title: UNDP ECoWYERT Program 2025–2030: Empowering Women, Youth, Entrepreneurs, and Traders for Regional Trade Growth Across Africa
summary: Unlock Business Growth, Trade Opportunities, and Entrepreneurship Skills Through the UNDP ECoWYERT Program Young people, entrepreneurs, traders, and enterprises across Southern and Central Africa now have a unique opportunity to build their skills, strengthen their businesses, and access regional trade opportunities through the Enhancing Capacities of Women and Youth-led Enterprises for Regional Trade (ECoWYERT) Program. Led by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, the ECoWYERT Program is designed to equip participants with practical skills, knowledge, and tools needed to thrive in an increasingly competitive regional and continental marketplace. The initiative seeks to support women and youth-led enterprises by providing market-oriented training that responds to the needs of individuals and businesses at different stages of development. Running from 2025 to 2030, the program aims to create pathways for economic empowerment, entrepreneurship development, employment creation, and increased participation in cross-border and regional trade throughout Africa. What is the ECoWYERT Program? The Enhancing Capacities of Women and Youth-led Enterprises for Regional Trade (ECoWYERT) Program is a regional initiative focused on improving the capabilities of youth, entrepreneurs, traders, and businesses to participate successfully in local, regional, and international trade. The program recognizes that participants operate at different levels of business maturity and therefore offers specialized training tailored to their current stage of employment, entrepreneurship, or trading journey. Whether an applicant is: Preparing to enter the workforce Launching a first business venture Managing an informal enterprise Trading across borders Growing a small business Expanding a medium-sized enterprise into regional markets the program is designed to provide relevant support to help them achieve sustainable growth. Organizations Behind the Initiative The ECoWYERT Program is implemented through a strategic partnership involving several leading development and trade organizations. Key partners include: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Mastercard Foundation COMESA Federation of Women in Business (COMFWB) Better Than Cash Alliance (BTCA) Trade and Development Fund (TDF) These organizations are working together to strengthen economic participation for women and youth and increase their involvement in regional trade and value chains. Countries Participating in the Program The ECoWYERT Program will be implemented across six African countries: Botswana Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Malawi South Africa Zambia Zimbabwe Participants from these countries will have access to training opportunities designed to improve employment prospects, entrepreneurial success, and regional trade engagement. Why the ECoWYERT Program Matters Africa s economic future depends heavily on the successful participation of young people, women entrepreneurs, traders, and small businesses. However, many face challenges such as: Limited access to business training Insufficient financial literacy Lack of formal business structures Limited market access Poor understanding of export requirements Limited exposure to regional trade opportunities The ECoWYERT Program seeks to address these challenges by equipping participants with practical and market-oriented skills that can enhance competitiveness and enable sustainable business growth. In addition, the program promotes awareness of opportunities available under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), helping participants understand how to access larger regional markets across Africa. Training Categories Available Applicants are required to choose the category that best represents their current stage of employment, business, or trade development. 1. New-to-Trade Youth This category targets young individuals who are beginning their entrepreneurial or employment journey. Eligible participants include: Young women and men aged 16 to 35 years Youth not in education, employment, or training (NEET) Aspiring entrepreneurs Recent graduates and trainees transitioning into employment Young people seeking to turn farming activities into viable businesses Youth engaged in income-generating activities who want to expand into sustainable enterprises Participants in this category will receive training in: Employability skills Entrepreneurship development Financial management Business fundamentals Introduction to regional trade Cross-border business opportunities 2. Existing Traders This category is designed for individuals already engaged in trading activities. Eligible applicants include: Sole traders Rural traders Peri-urban traders Small-Scale Cross-Border Traders (SSCBTs) Informal businesses Training areas include: Business management Financial record keeping Marketing techniques Customer engagement Digital business tools Business formalization Regional trade participation 3. Growing Trade Enterprises This category serves early-stage businesses that are looking to strengthen operations and prepare for expansion. Eligible applicants include: Micro-enterprises Small businesses Home-based businesses Small-scale processing enterprises Participants will benefit from training in: Business planning Financial management Marketing strategies Customer acquisition and retention Market access Trade readiness 4. Scaling Trade Enterprises This category targets established businesses seeking growth beyond local markets. Eligible applicants include: Medium-sized businesses Formal enterprises Business aggregators Growth-focused enterprises Training support includes: Export readiness Supply chain strengthening Advanced business systems Market expansion strategies Regional trade opportunities Expansion into continental markets Key Benefits of the ECoWYERT Program Depending on the category selected, participants will gain access to valuable skills and knowledge that can significantly improve their competitiveness and growth potential. Benefits include: Employment and Entrepreneurship Skills Participants will receive practical training that enhances their employability and entrepreneurial capabilities. Financial Literacy and Management The program provides important lessons in: Budgeting Financial planning Record keeping Cash flow management Business Growth Strategies Applicants will learn how to: Develop sustainable business models Increase profitability Improve operational efficiency Scale business activities Marketing and Customer Development Training covers: Customer engagement Branding strategies Sales techniques Market positioning Digital Business Skills Participants will gain exposure to modern digital tools that improve business performance and market reach. Business Formalization Support The program helps participants understand: Registration processes Compliance requirements Benefits of formal business operations Cross-Border Trade Knowledge Participants will learn how to: Access regional markets Engage in international trade Navigate trade requirements Explore export opportunities AfCFTA Market Opportunities The program introduces participants to opportunities available through the African Continental Free Trade Area, helping businesses position themselves for continental growth. How to Apply Interested and eligible applicants should complete the official application form and select the category that best reflects their current employment, business, or trade stage. CLICK HERE TO APPLY It is important to note that submission of an application does not guarantee selection. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. For more information about this program, CLICK HERE . Application Deadline Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. There is currently no fixed closing date announced. Interested applicants are advised to apply as early as possible to maximize their chances of consideration. Conclusion The UNDP ECoWYERT Program represents a significant opportunity for young people, women entrepreneurs, traders, and enterprises seeking to strengthen their skills and expand their economic potential. Through targeted, stage-specific training, participants will gain the knowledge, tools, and confidence needed to compete effectively in local, regional, and continental markets. By focusing on entrepreneurship development, business growth, trade readiness, financial management, and opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area, the program is helping build a future where youth and women-led enterprises can become key drivers of economic transformation across Africa. For aspiring entrepreneurs, informal traders, growing businesses, and established enterprises alike, the ECoWYERT Program offers a valuable pathway toward sustainable business success and regional trade integration. title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master’s in International Humanitarian Action 2027–2029: Scholarships, Eligibility, Study Structure and How to Apply
summary: The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master’s Degree Programme in International Humanitarian Action (NOHA) is a prestigious international postgraduate programme designed for graduates and professionals who want to build advanced academic knowledge and practical competencies for careers in humanitarian action, international cooperation, relief operations, policy, research and related fields. The programme is delivered through an international network of universities and combines multidisciplinary academic training, professional development, international mobility, research and practical exposure . The programme has a long history, having been established in 1993 with support from the European Commission, and has trained more than 3,500 graduates working in humanitarian relief and international cooperation around the world. The NOHA programme has also been selected again as an Erasmus Mundus programme , allowing it to continue offering Erasmus Mundus scholarships. The programme s official information indicates that the 2027–2029 cohort is open for applications . Erasmus Mundus Joint Master s in International Humanitarian Action 2027–2029 The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master s Degree Programme in International Humanitarian Action is an inter-university and multidisciplinary postgraduate programme focused specifically on humanitarian action. It is intended for people who are already working in humanitarian action as well as graduates and professionals who intend to develop careers in the humanitarian sector. Rather than limiting students to one institution or one national academic environment, the programme incorporates international mobility and enables students to study at different universities within the NOHA network. According to the programme description, the master s degree combines: Theoretical knowledge Analytical skills Professional competencies Practical and hands-on learning Interdisciplinary education International and multicultural exposure Research training Humanitarian specialisation International mobility This combination makes the programme particularly relevant to people interested in humanitarian relief, international development, humanitarian policy, forced migration, conflict, protection, resilience, humanitarian analysis and related areas. Why the NOHA Master s Programme Stands Out The NOHA Master s programme has several characteristics that distinguish it from a conventional master s degree. 1. A long-established humanitarian studies programme The programme was established in 1993 with support from the European Commission and is described by NOHA as the first master s programme in the area of humanitarian studies. Its approach combines academic and analytical training with practical learning, making it relevant to students who want to connect humanitarian theory with real-world humanitarian challenges. 2. International and multicultural learning environment NOHA brings together students and lecturers from different countries and academic backgrounds. The programme involves more than 150 in-house experts and field-experienced guest lecturers , while its alumni community includes more than 3,500 graduates working in humanitarian relief and international cooperation globally. This international environment can expose students to different perspectives on humanitarian crises, development challenges, conflict, displacement, disaster response and humanitarian governance. 3. Erasmus Mundus recognition and scholarship opportunities The programme was selected again as an Erasmus Mundus programme in 2025 and continues to offer Erasmus Mundus scholarships. For the 2027–2029 intake , NOHA states that the Erasmus Mundus scholarship allocation includes: 4 scholarships for candidates from Programme Countries 8 scholarships targeted at students from Partner Countries 4 scholarships for candidates from specified targeted regions The targeted regions identified by NOHA include Regions 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 under the Erasmus+ country classification. NOHA also states that no more than 10% of the total scholarships can be awarded to students of the same nationality , making the scholarship selection highly competitive. Programme Duration and Academic Structure The NOHA Joint Master s programme lasts two years , consisting of four semesters and 120 ECTS credits . The programme provides specialised education in humanitarian action while incorporating both academic and professional specialisations. Depending on the home and host university, students may study in English, French or Spanish . The programme is structured around four major stages. First Semester: Foundation Period The first semester is the Foundation Period , undertaken at the student s home university. Students receive broad interdisciplinary training designed to establish a common academic foundation for further specialisation. The official programme information places this period approximately from mid-to-late September through late January . Depending on the university, teaching may be conducted in English, French or Spanish. The English-language universities include: Ruhr-Universität Bochum, Germany University College Dublin, Ireland Uppsala University, Sweden Rijksuniversiteit Groningen, Netherlands University of Warsaw, Poland University of Malta, Malta French-language study is available at Aix-Marseille Université in France, while Spanish-language study is available at Universidad de Deusto in Spain. Second Semester: Specialisation Period During the second semester, students undertake a Specialisation Period at another NOHA university . This mobility component is one of the distinctive features of the programme. Students are expected to select their preferred universities and consider the specialisation offered by each institution when making their choices. The current NOHA programme identifies specialisations including: Resilience: Localising the Aid Effort – University College Dublin Forced Migration and Human Security – University of Malta Humanitarian Analysis and Intervention Design – Rijksuniversiteit Groningen Humanitarian Policy and Practice: From Delivering Aid to Ending Needs – Ruhr-Universität Bochum Armed Conflicts and Humanitarian Action – University of Warsaw Protection in Humanitarian Action – Universidad de Deusto Conflict, Peace-building and Religion – Uppsala University This allows students to develop expertise in an area that aligns with their professional interests and intended humanitarian career pathway. Third Semester: Contextualisation Period The third semester is the Contextualisation Period . Students can choose between different pathways, including regional training and a work-placement track. The regional training component allows students to explore humanitarian action within particular regional contexts, cooperate in different cultural settings and adapt their research interests to specific regional circumstances. NOHA identifies regional training opportunities involving partner institutions in locations including: Jordan Lebanon Qatar The programme also provides a Work Placement Track , allowing students to gain practical experience within a humanitarian organisation. Fourth Semester: Research Period The fourth semester is dedicated to the Research Period , during which students undertake their research and master s thesis. This provides an opportunity to integrate the knowledge and skills acquired during the preceding semesters into a substantial research project. The four-semester structure therefore provides a progression from broad humanitarian foundations to specialisation, contextualisation and independent research. The application for the 2027-2029 cohort is now open! Click here to apply International Mobility Is a Core Part of the Programme International mobility is not simply an optional feature of the NOHA programme. Students undertake compulsory physical mobility and must complete study periods in at least two countries , subject to the programme s mobility rules. The mandatory study periods must correspond to at least one academic semester each, and the required mobility cannot simply be replaced by virtual participation. This means applicants should be prepared for an academically and geographically mobile master s experience. Students should therefore consider: International travel Relocation between universities Visa requirements where applicable Different academic environments Cross-cultural learning Language requirements Accommodation and living arrangements The mobility structure is particularly valuable for applicants who want an international career in humanitarian affairs. Universities Delivering the NOHA Master s Programme The programme is delivered by a consortium of universities across Europe. The universities listed by NOHA include: Aix-Marseille Université, France University of Malta, Malta Rijksuniversiteit Groningen, Netherlands Ruhr-Universität Bochum, Germany Universidad de Deusto, Spain University College Dublin, Ireland University of Warsaw, Poland Uppsala University, Sweden The programme also works with partner universities outside the core consortium, including institutions in Thailand, Australia, the United States, Jordan, India, Colombia, Indonesia, Lebanon, Guatemala, Sierra Leone and Qatar. This extensive institutional network reinforces the programme s international and interdisciplinary character. Humanitarian Organisations Connected to the NOHA Network The NOHA network also has links with humanitarian and development organisations. The organisations listed on the programme page include: Action Against Hunger Restless Development Nepal Comhlámh Handicap International RedR UK Medici con l Africa – CUAMM Trust Consultancy Development Polish Humanitarian Action Croix-Rouge de Belgique IMPACT Initiatives METAdrasi INTERSOS Such connections are particularly relevant for students seeking to understand humanitarian action beyond the classroom and build professional networks within the sector. Who Should Consider Applying? The NOHA Master s programme is particularly suited to applicants who want to build or advance careers in humanitarian action. The programme explicitly targets people working or intending to work in the field of humanitarian action . Selection takes into account the applicant s education and professional background, experience and concern for humanitarian issues, multicultural sensitivity and linguistic abilities. Potential applicants may include graduates and professionals interested in areas such as: Humanitarian affairs International development International cooperation Disaster response Humanitarian policy Refugee and migration studies Conflict and peacebuilding Protection Humanitarian programme management Humanitarian research International relations Social sciences Public policy Development studies Emergency response Humanitarian logistics Community resilience Academic Background Required Applicants must generally hold a university first-cycle degree or bachelor s degree equivalent to at least 180 ECTS in a discipline relevant to humanitarian action. The programme identifies relevant academic areas including: Medical sciences Food sciences Economics and management Engineering Law Social sciences Education sciences Humanities The programme also states that candidates are assessed holistically, rather than solely on the basis of their academic qualification. Academic quality, professional experience, humanitarian interests, multicultural sensitivity and language abilities are among the factors considered during selection. Applicants should therefore demonstrate not only that they meet the formal academic requirements but also that their academic, professional and personal trajectory connects meaningfully with humanitarian action. Click here for more information on Erasmus Mundus Scholarships for 2027-2029 Erasmus Mundus Scholarships for 2027–2029 One of the major attractions of the programme is the availability of Erasmus Mundus scholarships. For the 2027–2029 intake, NOHA indicates the availability of 16 Erasmus Mundus scholarships , distributed across Programme Countries, Partner Countries and specified targeted regions. The scholarship allocation is competitive, and the programme states that no more than 10% of the total scholarships can be awarded to candidates of the same nationality. Applicants should distinguish between: Admission to the master s programme , and Selection for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship Meeting the academic admission requirements does not automatically guarantee an Erasmus Mundus scholarship. The scholarship application has its own deadline and documentation requirements. Application Deadlines For the 2027–2029 cohort , the official NOHA information identifies the following key deadlines: Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline 15 December 2026 This is the key deadline for applicants seeking consideration for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship. General application deadline 1 April 2027 This is the central application deadline for ordinary/self-funded applicants according to the current NOHA programme information. Applicants without EU citizenship or a valid EU residence permit 1 July 2027 The current NOHA timeline identifies a further deadline for applicants without EU citizenship or a valid EU residence permit. Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the programme s current instructions because university-specific requirements can affect the application process. The supplied programme page states the application is open for the 2027–2029 cohort and provides the Erasmus Mundus grant deadline as 15 December . What Students Gain From the Programme The NOHA programme offers more than a conventional classroom-based master s degree. Students can gain: Advanced knowledge of international humanitarian action Interdisciplinary academic training Professional competencies for humanitarian work Exposure to multiple universities and countries Experience working across cultures Opportunities for specialisation Research and analytical skills Potential practical experience through work placement Access to an international alumni network Exposure to humanitarian practitioners and experts Preparation for careers in humanitarian relief and international cooperation The programme s alumni have gone on to work in humanitarian organisations, international institutions, research organisations, development agencies and other professional settings. NOHA highlights an alumni community of more than 3,500 graduates working internationally. Career Opportunities After the NOHA Master s Graduates of a specialised master s degree in humanitarian action can potentially pursue professional pathways in areas such as: Humanitarian programme management Emergency response Humanitarian policy International development Refugee and migration programming Protection Conflict and peacebuilding Monitoring and evaluation Humanitarian research Programme coordination Disaster risk reduction International cooperation Humanitarian advocacy Development and relief operations Research and academia The programme is specifically designed to develop personnel capable of working across different levels of humanitarian relief operations and contributing to professional humanitarian assistance and sustainable action. A Truly International Academic Experience A major strength of the NOHA programme is its international character. Students do not simply study humanitarian action as an abstract academic discipline. The programme places humanitarian questions within different geographical, political, social and institutional contexts. The combination of home-university study, specialisation at another university, contextualisation and research enables students to examine humanitarian issues from multiple perspectives. This is particularly important because humanitarian crises are rarely confined to one discipline. A contemporary humanitarian response may involve: Public administration International relations Law Economics Public health Engineering Social sciences Education Conflict studies Migration studies Disaster management Environmental considerations Community development The interdisciplinary design of NOHA reflects this complexity. International Network and Alumni Community NOHA is supported by a broad international academic and professional network. The network currently describes itself as an international association of universities focused on enhancing professionalism in the humanitarian sector through education and training, research and publications, and projects . It includes universities and partner institutions from Europe and other parts of the world. The alumni network is another important component of the programme. Testimonials from former students describe the value of NOHA in developing: Critical thinking Analytical skills Interdisciplinary thinking Cross-cultural collaboration Practical understanding Professional networks Research capabilities Understanding of different humanitarian perspectives The programme s international alumni community can therefore provide an important professional network for graduates pursuing careers across borders. Important Considerations Before Applying Prospective applicants should carefully consider several issues before submitting an application. 1. The scholarship is highly competitive The number of Erasmus Mundus scholarships is limited relative to the international applicant pool. Applicants should therefore ensure that their application clearly demonstrates academic strength, relevant experience, humanitarian motivation and international or multicultural awareness. 2. Mobility is compulsory Applicants should be comfortable studying in multiple countries and adapting to different academic and cultural environments. 3. Language requirements matter Applicants should identify the language requirements associated with their preferred universities before submitting their choices. 4. University-specific requirements may apply Some NOHA universities have additional national requirements. These can affect admission and must be checked carefully before application. 5. Admission and scholarship selection are different An applicant can potentially be academically suitable for the master s programme without being selected for an Erasmus Mundus scholarship. This distinction is important when planning applications and finances. Who Can Apply? The programme is designed for graduates and professionals from a wide range of academic and professional backgrounds who are interested in humanitarian action. There is no race-based restriction stated in the programme s eligibility requirements . NOHA describes an international student body and assesses candidates partly through factors such as nationality and gender balance. For the master s programme, applicants generally need a bachelor s degree or equivalent first-cycle university qualification of at least 180 ECTS in a field relevant to humanitarian action. Relevant backgrounds include social sciences, humanities, law, economics and management, engineering, medical sciences, food sciences and education sciences. The Erasmus Mundus scholarship component uses Erasmus+ classifications of Programme Countries, Partner Countries and specified targeted regions. Under the current Erasmus+ classification, Ghana is included in Region 9: Sub-Saharan Africa , alongside numerous other African countries. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to qualified applicants from Ghana and other eligible countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, subject to the specific Erasmus Mundus scholarship rules and the programme s competitive selection process. Conclusion The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master s Degree Programme in International Humanitarian Action represents a major opportunity for graduates and professionals seeking advanced international training in humanitarian affairs. Its combination of 120 ECTS of postgraduate study, multidisciplinary teaching, international mobility, specialised learning, contextual training, research, professional exposure and access to an international humanitarian network makes it particularly relevant to individuals seeking careers in humanitarian action, international development, relief operations, policy, research and international cooperation. For applicants interested in the Erasmus Mundus scholarship, the most important date is 15 December 2026 . Those seeking admission as ordinary or self-funded applicants should also pay attention to the 1 April 2027 central application deadline and the 1 July 2027 deadline identified for applicants without EU citizenship or a valid EU residence permit. Because the scholarship is highly competitive, prospective applicants should begin preparing their academic documents, language evidence, professional documentation, motivation materials and other supporting evidence well before the deadline. The opportunity is especially significant for applicants from regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa , including Ghana, who meet the academic and programme requirements and want to develop an internationally oriented career in humanitarian action. title: KNUST–Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf Exchange Scholarship 2027: Apply for Up to €4,670 to Study in Germany
summary: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, in partnership with Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU), Germany, has announced a Call for Nominations for the HHU Exchange Scholarship for the Summer Semester 2027. The opportunity is designed for eligible KNUST Bachelor s and Master s students who wish to undertake an academic exchange at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf during the Summer Semester 2027, which runs from April to September 2027. Successful applicants can receive financial support of up to €934 per month for a maximum of five months, with total funding of up to €4,670. The scholarship provides an opportunity for students to gain international academic exposure, experience studying in Germany, develop international networks and broaden their academic and professional perspectives. Important: This is a partial scholarship. Students should be prepared to cover expenses that are not fully covered by the scholarship. Opportunity Overview Opportunity: HHU Exchange Scholarship Host University: Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU), Germany Home University: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi Study Period: Summer Semester 2027 Exchange Period: April – September 2027 Funding: Up to €934 per month Maximum Funding Period: 5 months Maximum Total Funding: Up to €4,670 Application Deadline: Tuesday, 13 October 2026 at 5:00 PM Application Method: Online application form Scholarship Type: Partial scholarship Contact Email: international-partners@hhu.de About the HHU Exchange Scholarship Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf is inviting eligible students through its exchange partnership with KNUST to participate in an academic exchange during the Summer Semester 2027. The programme provides students with an opportunity to spend part of their academic programme at a German university while gaining exposure to a different academic environment and international community. For KNUST students, an exchange experience at HHU can provide more than classroom learning. Studying abroad can expose participants to different teaching and learning approaches, international research environments, cultural perspectives and professional networks. The exchange can also help students develop greater independence, adaptability and cross-cultural communication skills while studying in an international environment. Who Can Apply? The call is specifically directed at eligible Bachelor s and Master s students at KNUST who qualify for participation in the exchange programme. Applicants should: Be enrolled as a Bachelor s or Master s student at KNUST. Meet the relevant academic and exchange requirements. Be able to provide the required academic and supporting documents. Be able to obtain the required confirmation of academic supervision from an HHU lecturer. Be prepared to participate in the Summer Semester 2027 exchange period. Nationality and Country Eligibility The announcement does not specify a particular racial restriction or nationality quota. The opportunity is presented as an exchange programme between KNUST in Ghana and Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf in Germany. Therefore, the primary eligibility consideration is the applicant s status as an eligible KNUST student. Primary eligible institution: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana. Exchange destination: Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, Germany. Applicants should confirm their individual eligibility and nomination status with the relevant KNUST authorities before applying. Scholarship Benefits and Funding One of the major benefits of the HHU Exchange Scholarship is the financial support available to successful applicants during their exchange period. Up to €934 Per Month Successful applicants may receive up to €934 per month during the funded exchange period. Up to Five Months of Funding The scholarship can provide funding for a maximum period of five months. Up to €4,670 in Total If the full five-month funding period is awarded at the maximum monthly amount, the total scholarship support can reach: €934 × 5 months = €4,670 This can provide substantial financial assistance towards the cost of living during the exchange. Important: This Is a Partial Scholarship Applicants should not assume that the scholarship will cover every cost associated with studying in Germany. The KNUST announcement explicitly describes the funding as a partial scholarship and advises students to be prepared to cover the remaining expenses. HHU estimates living costs in Düsseldorf at approximately €1,000–€1,600 per month . Students may therefore need additional funds to cover expenses such as: Accommodation Food and daily living expenses Transportation Travel to and from Germany Visa-related expenses, where applicable Insurance Personal expenses Academic or administrative expenses that may not be covered Any difference between actual living expenses and the scholarship allowance Application Requirements Applicants are required to prepare several documents before completing the application. The KNUST announcement lists the following requirements. 1. Copy of Academic Transcript Applicants must provide a copy of their academic transcript. The transcript demonstrates the applicant s academic record and allows the relevant authorities to assess the student s academic standing. Applicants should ensure that the transcript is clear, complete and readable. 2. Copy of Bachelor s Degree Certificate A copy of the Bachelor s degree certificate is listed among the required documents. This requirement is particularly relevant to Master s students and applicants who have already completed their Bachelor s degree. Applicants should ensure that the certificate is properly scanned and legible. 3. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV). The CV should clearly present the applicant s academic background, relevant experience, skills, achievements and other information that supports the exchange application. Applicants should ensure that their CV is professional, well structured and up to date. 4. Passport Biodata Page Applicants must provide a copy of the biodata page of their passport. This is the page containing the applicant s personal information and photograph. The copy should be clear and all information should be readable. 5. Motivation Letter A motivation letter is required as part of the application. The motivation letter gives applicants an opportunity to explain why they are interested in participating in the exchange programme and why they should be considered for the scholarship. A strong motivation letter should explain: The applicant s academic interests. Reasons for wanting to study at HHU. How the exchange relates to the applicant s current programme. What the applicant hopes to gain from the exchange. How the international experience could contribute to their academic and professional development. Why the applicant is a strong candidate for the opportunity. Applicants should avoid submitting a generic motivation letter. The letter should be specifically tailored to the HHU exchange opportunity. 6. Recommendation Letter Applicants are expected to provide a recommendation letter. According to the announcement, the recommendation letter is preferably from the Head of Department (HoD), although it is not mandatory. Applicants who are able to obtain an appropriate recommendation from their HoD should consider doing so while following any additional instructions provided by KNUST. 7. Confirmation of Academic Supervision from an HHU Lecturer Applicants must provide confirmation of academic supervision from an HHU lecturer. This is an important part of the application because it demonstrates an academic connection or supervision arrangement at the host institution. Applicants should therefore pay close attention to this requirement and ensure that the necessary confirmation is obtained before submitting the application. Application Documents Must Be Combined Into One PDF An important instruction in the announcement is that applicants should combine all required documents into a single PDF file for uploading. A recommended order could be: Academic transcript Bachelor s degree certificate Curriculum Vitae Passport biodata page Motivation letter Recommendation letter, where available Confirmation of academic supervision from an HHU lecturer Applicants should follow the official application instructions carefully in case KNUST provides a preferred document order or additional requirements. How to Apply Interested and eligible applicants are required to complete the online application form. The application form is accessed through the link encoded in the QR code included on the official KNUST announcement. Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility Ensure that you are an eligible KNUST Bachelor s or Master s student and that you meet the relevant exchange requirements. Step 2: Prepare Your Documents Gather all required supporting documents, including your academic transcript, degree certificate, CV, passport biodata page, motivation letter and other required confirmations. Step 3: Obtain Academic Supervision Confirmation Contact the relevant HHU academic contact or lecturer and secure the required confirmation of academic supervision. Step 4: Combine Your Documents Combine all required documents into one PDF file, as instructed in the announcement. Step 5: Complete the Online Application Complete the application form accurately and upload the required single PDF file. Step 6: Submit Before the Deadline Ensure that your completed application is submitted before 5:00 PM on Tuesday, 13 October 2026 . Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final hours to submit their applications because technical difficulties, incomplete documents or delays in obtaining required confirmations could prevent timely submission. Application Deadline The deadline for the KNUST–HHU Exchange Scholarship is: Tuesday, 13 October 2026 at 5:00 PM Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. Late applications may not be considered. Study Period: Summer Semester 2027 Successful applicants will participate during the Summer Semester 2027 , covering the period from April to September 2027. The exchange period provides students with the opportunity to experience academic life at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf while studying within an international environment. The exact academic schedule, courses and arrangements may vary depending on the student s programme and academic department. Applicants should therefore remain in contact with the relevant KNUST and HHU exchange coordinators for further information about their specific exchange arrangements. Why Consider This Exchange Opportunity? Participating in an international exchange can provide several academic, personal and professional advantages. International Academic Exposure Students can experience a different university environment and interact with academics and students from different backgrounds. This can broaden their understanding of their field and expose them to different approaches to teaching, learning and research. Experience Studying in Germany The exchange provides eligible KNUST students with an opportunity to experience higher education in Germany and gain international academic exposure. Professional Networking Students can build relationships with academics, researchers and fellow students from different countries. These connections can potentially contribute to future academic, research and professional opportunities. Personal Development Living and studying abroad can strengthen independence, adaptability, communication skills, confidence and cross-cultural awareness. Academic Collaboration Students can be exposed to different academic approaches, research environments and opportunities for collaboration. International Experience for Your CV An international academic exchange can strengthen a student s CV by demonstrating adaptability, international exposure, cultural awareness and the ability to study and operate in a new academic environment. Financial Planning for Students Although the scholarship provides significant financial assistance, applicants should carefully consider the difference between the scholarship amount and the estimated cost of living. HHU estimates living expenses in Düsseldorf at approximately €1,000–€1,600 per month , while the scholarship provides up to €934 per month . This means students may need additional funds to meet their actual monthly expenses. For example, if a student s living expenses reach €1,300 in a particular month and they receive the maximum €934 scholarship, there would be a difference of approximately €366 that would need to be covered through other available resources. Actual expenses will vary depending on accommodation, lifestyle, transportation and other personal circumstances. Students are therefore advised to prepare a realistic financial plan before accepting an exchange placement. About Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) is a major university located in Düsseldorf, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. The university hosts international students and maintains partnerships with institutions around the world. HHU s international activities include exchange arrangements with partner universities, providing students with opportunities to undertake study periods abroad and gain international academic experience. The university also has an International Office responsible for international student and exchange-related matters. About KNUST The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is based in Kumasi, Ghana, and is one of Ghana s leading universities. The university s International Programmes Office plays an important role in supporting international academic engagement and exchange activities. title: SNSF Starting Grants 2027: CHF 1 Million Research Grant for Independent Researchers to Lead a Research Team in Switzerland
summary: The SNSF Starting Grants 2027 offer an exceptional research funding opportunity for researchers ready to establish themselves as independent research leaders in Switzerland. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) , the programme enables researchers to carry out an independent research project and build and lead a research team in Switzerland. The SNSF Starting Grants represent the SNSF’s highest level of career funding and are open to all research disciplines and topics . Successful applicants can receive up to CHF 1 million in project funding for a maximum period of five years , with additional funding potentially available to cover the applicant’s own salary where the eligibility conditions are met. For the 2027 call, applications open on 1 February 2027 , with the final submission deadline set for 4 May 2027 at 17:00 CET (Swiss local time) . About the SNSF Starting Grants 2027 The SNSF Starting Grants are designed for researchers who are moving towards an established level of scientific independence. The programme supports researchers who are ready to develop and conduct their own research, attract research funding and take responsibility for a research team. The goal is not simply to finance another research project. The grant is intended to support researchers at a significant career transition: from demonstrating scientific independence to becoming established research leaders who can make a substantial contribution to their field. Applicants are therefore expected to demonstrate significant research achievements since obtaining their PhD, medical degree or equivalent qualification. They should have produced original research outputs that have undergone appropriate quality assurance and should be able to design, plan and conduct their proposed project without supervision. The SNSF also expects applicants to demonstrate a broad research network and experience in mentoring or supporting less experienced researchers in academic or extra-academic environments. SNSF Starting Grants 2027 Benefits One of the major attractions of the SNSF Starting Grants 2027 is the scale of funding available to successful researchers. Up to CHF 1 Million in Project Funding Applicants can request a maximum of CHF 1 million in project funds for a project lasting up to five years. The project budget can support costs directly related to achieving the research objectives, including project staff, equipment, research materials, travel, conferences, workshops, research data access, infrastructure use and other eligible research expenses. Additional Salary Funding Researchers who need funding for their own salary may request their salary in addition to the project funds . This means the CHF 1 million ceiling applies to project funding; it does not necessarily represent the total amount that an eligible applicant can receive when their own salary is also funded. Applicants who already have an appropriate secured position for the full duration of the grant generally request project funding only. Five-Year Research Project The SNSF Starting Grant can support a project for a maximum of five years . Projects that are shorter than five years receive a correspondingly reduced budget based on the duration of the project. Independence and Research Leadership The grant is designed to help researchers establish themselves as independent research leaders. Host institutions must provide conditions that allow the grantee to manage the project, research funds and team independently, while also providing access to appropriate infrastructure, equipment and other institutional resources. Open to All Research Disciplines The SNSF Starting Grants 2027 are not restricted to one academic field. Researchers from all disciplines and research topics can apply, provided they satisfy the personal, formal and scientific requirements of the call. Who Can Apply for the SNSF Starting Grants 2027? The SNSF Starting Grants are intended for researchers who are at the R3 career stage , meaning they are moving towards the level of an established independent researcher. Applicants must already have demonstrated scientific independence but must not have reached the level that the Starting Grant is designed to support. To be considered, applicants must satisfy all three personal eligibility requirements by 4 May 2027 : The eligibility window requirement The career-stage requirement The Swiss-link requirement In addition, applicants must hold a qualifying academic or professional qualification. Academic Qualifications Required Applicants must hold one of the following: A PhD A medical degree A qualification equivalent to a PhD The SNSF evaluates the applicant’s research experience and qualifications according to the rules established in the call document. Eligibility Window for PhD Holders Researchers applying on the basis of a PhD must satisfy specific research-experience and timing requirements. Applicants must have: At least two years of research experience after the PhD defence An average workload of at least 0.8 FTE during the relevant research experience Their application must be submitted no more than eight years after the PhD defence The research experience may be obtained in an academic or extra-academic research environment. The relevant period is calculated from the oral defence of the relevant degree up to 4 May 2027 . Eligibility for Applicants with a Medical Degree Applicants applying on the basis of a medical degree have a different eligibility framework. They must have: At least three years of clinical work At least two years of research experience Research experience undertaken at an average workload of at least 0.8 FTE An application submitted no more than 12 years after the medical degree The SNSF also takes into consideration the appropriate research activities associated with medical training when evaluating research achievements. Eligibility Through a Qualification Equivalent to a PhD Researchers who hold a qualification equivalent to a PhD can also apply. For this route, the qualification is defined in the call document as involving three years of research activity at an average workload of 0.8 FTE after a higher education degree . Applicants must then have at least two additional years of research experience at an average of 0.8 FTE and must submit their application no more than eight years after obtaining the equivalent qualification. Can the Eligibility Window Be Extended? Yes, an extension may be possible in certain circumstances. The SNSF permits extensions of the eligibility window for reasons covered under the relevant SNSF General Implementation Regulations. However, an extension is not automatic . It must be approved by the SNSF Administrative Office. Applicants requesting an extension should contact the SNSF at stg@snf.ch and provide the relevant supporting documentation before submitting their application. Career Stage Requirement Applicants must be at the R3 career stage . The purpose of the SNSF Starting Grant is to help researchers transition into an established independent research leadership position. Consequently, researchers who have already achieved this objective are not eligible. An applicant is considered to have already reached the objective if, by the application deadline, they are already leading an independent research group of approximately two to three people, typically exceeding 2.0 FTE. The objective can also be considered achieved when an applicant already holds, or has a binding agreement for, a position that enables them to lead their own research group and they have already received or been awarded significant funding from their institution, the SNSF or another funding source. These are benchmarks, so applicants who are uncertain about their situation are encouraged to contact the SNSF before submitting. Swiss-Link Requirement A particularly important requirement for international researchers is the Swiss-link . The SNSF does not provide a simple country-based eligibility list. Instead, applicants must demonstrate a qualifying connection with Switzerland through at least one of the following routes: 1. Research Employment in Switzerland The applicant has been employed in a research position equivalent to at least two years , with an average workload of at least 80% (0.8 FTE) , at a Swiss research institution in the higher education sector in Switzerland. 2. Swiss Nationality The applicant is a Swiss national . 3. Swiss Higher Education Degree The applicant holds a qualifying degree from a Swiss higher education institution, including a: Master’s degree PhD MD/FMH Equivalent qualification The call document specifies that international organisations located in Switzerland, such as CERN, do not by themselves satisfy the Swiss-link requirement unless the applicant also has an appropriate affiliation with a Swiss higher education institution. Therefore, international researchers can apply, but they must satisfy one of the SNSF’s specified Swiss-link conditions. Who Is Not Eligible? Researchers who have already reached the independent research leadership level targeted by the Starting Grants cannot apply. Applicants must also pay attention to restrictions concerning other SNSF funding applications and existing grants. For example, applicants cannot normally have another SNSF application under evaluation when the requested funding periods overlap, although exceptions exist for one-off calls such as National Research Programmes and National Centres of Competence in Research. Importantly, researchers who submit an Ambizione application under the 2026 call cannot apply for the SNSF Starting Grants 2027 . Can You Apply for the SNSF Starting Grant More Than Once? Yes, but only under a specific limit. If an SNSF Starting Grant proposal is rejected after evaluation, the applicant may submit one further Starting Grant application . This second application may concern: The same project, revised; or An entirely new project. The topic and ranking of the previous application do not determine whether the applicant can make the second submission. Each proposal is evaluated independently. Can You Apply for an ERC Starting Grant at the Same Time? Parallel applications to other non-SNSF funding schemes, including ERC Starting Grants , are permitted. However, double funding is not permitted. If another substantial R3-level career grant is approved while the SNSF Starting Grant application is being evaluated, the applicant must inform the SNSF and choose between accepting the other grant or continuing with the SNSF evaluation. Host Institution Requirements A successful SNSF Starting Grant must be hosted by an eligible higher education or research institution in Switzerland. The host institution must be established in Switzerland as a legal entity under Swiss law and must provide a signed confirmation letter with the application. The applicant does not necessarily have to be employed by the host institution when submitting the application. However, the institution must employ the applicant for the duration of the project if the grant is awarded. Depending on the type of institution, the host must provide an appropriate independent position. Higher education institutions with professorial positions must offer at least an assistant professor-level position for the duration of the grant. Research institutions without professorial positions must offer a group leader position that provides independent project and management responsibility. The host institution must also guarantee appropriate working space, professional integration, access to infrastructure and equipment, and independence in managing the research project, funds and team. Work-Time and Employment Requirements Applicants should discuss employment conditions with their proposed host institution before submitting the application. The specific work-time requirements depend on whether the applicant requests funding for their own salary and on their type of institution or professional position. For applicants with a guaranteed qualifying position and no salary request, the employment level must generally be at least 0.5 FTE , with at least 0.5 FTE devoted to the project. For applicants requesting their own salary, different rules apply. For example, in most cases applicants must be employed at least 0.8 FTE and dedicate at least 80% of their working time to the project . University of applied sciences and teacher-education applicants have specific requirements, while clinician scientists have a separate employment arrangement reflecting their clinical responsibilities. What Does the SNSF Starting Grant Cover? The funding request must be directly connected to the research project and appropriately justified. Eligible project expenses can include: Salaries for doctoral researchers Postdoctoral researchers Other project staff Travel Conferences Workshops Research data access Equipment Research materials Consumables Infrastructure use Data procurement Equipment costing more than CHF 100,000 may be permitted provided the overall project budget remains within the CHF 1 million project-funding limit. Applicants must declare all relevant available resources and funding from their host institution, the SNSF and third parties. Application Process for the SNSF Starting Grants 2027 Applications are submitted entirely through the SNSF Portal . Applicants who do not already have an SNSF Portal account should create one well before the deadline. The call document recommends registering at least one month before the submission deadline . The application is submitted in one submission step and must include the mandatory host confirmation. Step 1: Check Your Eligibility Before preparing the full proposal, applicants should confirm that they satisfy: The required academic qualification The eligibility window The R3 career-stage requirement The Swiss-link requirement The restrictions concerning other SNSF grants and applications The host institution requirements Applicants who are uncertain about their eligibility should contact the SNSF Administrative Office before submitting. Step 2: Create or Update Your SNSF Portal Account Applications must be submitted through the SNSF Portal. Applicants without an account should register early because the SNSF recommends creating an account at least one month before the deadline. Step 3: Select a Host Institution The applicant must identify an eligible Swiss higher education or research institution willing to host the project. The institution must provide the required confirmation letter, signed by the vice-rector responsible for research or an equivalent authority. Step 4: Prepare the Research Proposal The research plan is a central part of the application. It must clearly explain: The research objectives The scientific problem How the project goes beyond the current state of knowledge The hypotheses or theoretical basis where relevant The proposed methodology How the research will generate new knowledge How the project will be implemented The expected outputs and outcomes Research objectives should be measurable and clearly defined. Step 5: Prepare the Research Plan The research plan must be written in English and may contain a maximum of 15 A4 pages and 60,000 characters including spaces . The formatting requirements include: At least 10-point font 1.5 line spacing At least 2 cm margins A standard readable font such as Times New Roman or Arial PDF format The research plan must be legible and comply with the SNSF s formal requirements. Step 6: Prepare the CV and Major Achievements Applicants must complete the SNSF CV. The evaluation considers the applicant s research qualification while taking disciplinary context and academic age into account. Importantly, the SNSF follows principles associated with DORA , meaning that the quality, value and impact of major research achievements are more important than relying simply on publication counts or journal names. Major achievements can include different forms of research output, such as datasets, software and prototypes, depending on the discipline. Step 7: Provide the Required Degree Documentation Applicants must upload official documentation confirming their PhD, medical degree or equivalent qualification. The documentation must show the date of the oral defence or examination, or this date must be established through a separate document. If the qualification documents are not in an official Swiss language or English, a certified translation is required. Step 8: Complete the Budget Applicants must provide a detailed and justified budget. The requested funds should be proportionate to the project s objectives and accurately reflect the resources required. All funding already available or requested from other sources must also be declared. Step 9: Complete the Declarations Applicants must declare relevant ethical issues, comply with applicable laws and ethical standards, and follow scientific-integrity requirements. The application must also address open access and research data requirements. Successful applicants must ensure open access to peer-reviewed publications, while research data should be made publicly accessible through FAIR-compliant repositories where legal, ethical and copyright considerations permit. Evaluation Process The SNSF Starting Grants 2027 use a two-phase competitive evaluation process . Phase 1: Thematic Panel Evaluation In the first phase, proposals are assessed by thematic panels. At least two panel members independently evaluate each proposal and provide structured recommendations. The panel then discusses the proposals and determines which applications proceed to the next stage. Some applications may be rejected after this first evaluation. Phase 2: External Peer Review and Interview Applications that progress to Phase 2 undergo external peer review. Applicants may request the exclusion of specific researchers from the peer-review process when there is a valid and justified reason and alternative reviewers are available. Applicants are also invited to an interview, where they present their project and answer questions. The proposals are subsequently rated and ranked. The SNSF Programme Committee Careers makes the final funding decisions within the available budget. In cases where proposals are tied around the funding threshold, random selection may be used. How Are Applications Evaluated? The SNSF identifies two broad areas of evaluation. Scientific Quality Reviewers consider the: Groundbreaking nature and potential impact of the research Importance of the research challenge Ambition of the project Extent to which it goes beyond the state of the art Novelty of concepts and approaches Interdisciplinary potential where relevant Scientific approach and methodology Feasibility Work arrangements and timeline Adequacy of resources Applicant s commitment to the project Applicant Qualification The applicant is assessed for their: Intellectual capacity Creativity Ability to conduct groundbreaking research Creative and original thinking Scientific expertise Capacity to carry out the proposed research SNSF Starting Grants 2027 Important Dates Applicants should carefully note the official 2027 timeline. Event Date Call opens 1 February 2027 Application deadline 4 May 2027, 17:00 CET Evaluation Phase 1 May–October 2027 Phase 1 outcome End of October 2027 Phase 1 decision letters November 2027 Evaluation Phase 2 October 2027–February 2028 SSH interviews 27–28 January 2028 LS interviews 3–4 February 2028 MINT interviews 10–11 February 2028 Phase 2 outcome End of March 2028 Phase 2 decision letters April 2028 Earliest grant start 1 May 2028 Latest grant start 1 May 2029 The SNSF notes that the timeline is subject to change, so applicants should consult the official Starting Grants information before making final arrangements. What Happens After the Application? After submission, the SNSF carries out administrative checks to verify formal and personal eligibility as well as the eligibility of the host institution. Applicants can follow the status of their application through the SNSF Portal. Importantly, the SNSF may determine that an application is ineligible even after the evaluation process has started if an eligibility problem is identified. Applicants who are unsuccessful receive decision letters. Depending on the evaluation phase reached, applicants may receive scientific reasons, anonymised referee assessments and, in Phase 2, external peer-review assessments. Highly ranked proposals that cannot be funded immediately may also be placed on a Funding Reserve List , depending on available funding. What Makes the SNSF Starting Grants 2027 Valuable? The SNSF Starting Grants 2027 are particularly significant because they combine substantial research funding with an opportunity to establish scientific independence. Rather than simply providing a small project grant, the programme is designed around the development of a researcher into an independent research leader. Successful applicants are expected to lead their own team, manage research resources and make a substantial contribution to their field. For researchers who have already accumulated significant research experience but have not yet reached the established independent researcher stage, this makes the SNSF Starting Grant an important career-development opportunity. Key Points Applicants Should Remember Before submitting an SNSF Starting Grants 2027 application, prospective applicants should remember the following: The call opens on 1 February 2027 . The deadline is 4 May 2027 at 17:00 CET . The opportunity is open to all research disciplines and topics . Applicants need a PhD, medical degree or equivalent qualification . PhD applicants generally need at least two years of research experience and must apply within eight years of their PhD defence. Medical applicants have separate clinical and research-experience requirements. Applicants must meet the R3 career-stage requirement . Applicants must have a qualifying Swiss-link . Applicants can request up to CHF 1 million in project funding . Own salary funding may be available in addition to project funds where the conditions are met. Projects can run for up to five years . Applications are submitted through the SNSF Portal . A qualifying Swiss host institution and signed host confirmation are required. The proposal must be prepared in English . The research plan has a maximum of 15 A4 pages and 60,000 characters including spaces . The evaluation consists of two phases , including panel assessment, external peer review and interviews. A previously rejected Starting Grant applicant may submit one further application . The official 2027 interview period is scheduled for January and February 2028, depending on the research field. How to Apply for SNSF Starting Grants 2027 Eligible researchers should prepare their application carefully and submit all required information and documents through the SNSF Portal before the deadline. Application Portal: SNSF Portal Applications must be submitted no later than 4 May 2027 at 17:00 CET, Swiss local time . Applicants should ensure that all required documents have been uploaded before the deadline because incomplete submissions may not be considered. The SNSF Starting Grants 2027 provide a major research funding opportunity for researchers ready to take the next step towards independent scientific leadership in Switzerland. With up to CHF 1 million in project funding , support for eligible applicants own salaries, projects of up to five years and opportunities to establish and lead a research team, the programme is designed for researchers with strong scientific achievements and clear potential for groundbreaking research. Because eligibility depends on the applicant s research experience, career stage, qualification and Swiss-link , prospective applicants should review the official requirements carefully before preparing their proposal. Researchers who meet the requirements should also begin discussions with their prospective host institution well ahead of the 4 May 2027 deadline . title: AIxBio Fellowship 2027 in Cambridge: Fully Funded 10-Week Programme for AI, Biosecurity, Research, Policy and Technology Professionals
summary: The AIxBio Fellowship 2027 is offering an intensive, fully funded opportunity for researchers, engineers, policy professionals, entrepreneurs and technically minded individuals interested in tackling important challenges at the intersection of advanced artificial intelligence and biosecurity . Organised by ERA in partnership with the Cambridge Biosecurity Hub , the 10-week, full-time programme will take place in Cambridge, United Kingdom , from 18 January to 26 March 2027 . The fellowship is designed for people who want to work on some of the most important emerging challenges associated with increasingly capable AI and biological risks, including the potential for AI to amplify biological threats and global catastrophic biological risks. Importantly, applicants do not need prior formal research experience to apply. The programme welcomes individuals from a wide range of backgrounds, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, software engineering, biology, policy, governance, security and entrepreneurship. Successful fellows will receive a £10,000 total stipend , together with expert mentorship, research management, workshops, networking opportunities and operational support throughout the programme. About the AIxBio Fellowship 2027 The AIxBio Fellowship is a specialised programme focused on the rapidly developing relationship between artificial intelligence and biosecurity . As AI systems become increasingly capable, they may create both opportunities and risks in biological research and security. The fellowship aims to bring talented people from different technical and professional backgrounds together to work on problems that could help reduce serious biological risks. The programme is particularly concerned with global catastrophic biological risks (GCBRs) , including risks associated with engineered pandemics and biological threats that could potentially be amplified by advanced AI. Rather than being limited to one academic discipline, the fellowship is deliberately interdisciplinary. It can accommodate projects and work involving: Artificial intelligence Machine learning AI safety Biological AI Biosecurity Biological risk reduction Biosecurity safeguards Policy Governance Security Technology implementation Research Entrepreneurship Other related areas at the AI-biosecurity intersection This interdisciplinary approach means that the programme can be relevant to people who approach biosecurity from technical, scientific, policy, governance, security or entrepreneurial perspectives. Who Is the AIxBio Fellowship Designed For? The programme welcomes a broad range of applicants who are interested in addressing important problems involving AI and biosecurity. Potential applicants include: Graduate students Early-career researchers Experienced researchers AI and machine-learning professionals Software engineers Biologists Policy researchers Governance professionals Security professionals Entrepreneurs and founders Technically minded generalists Professionals working on AI safety Individuals interested in biological security Professionals working at the intersection of technology and public policy The programme is particularly interested in people who can bring useful expertise, technical skills, research abilities, policy knowledge or entrepreneurial thinking to important AI-biosecurity problems. No Prior Formal Research Experience Required One of the notable features of the AIxBio Fellowship is that prior formal research experience is not required . This makes the programme potentially accessible to people who have strong technical, professional or interdisciplinary backgrounds but have not yet established a traditional academic research career. While previous research experience can be useful, applicants are not required to have an extensive publication record or formal research background. Instead, applicants can demonstrate their potential through their: Technical abilities Problem-solving skills Professional experience Research interests Policy experience Entrepreneurial experience Understanding of AI or biology Interest in biosecurity Ability to work on complex interdisciplinary problems Motivation to address global catastrophic biological risks What Is the Main Focus of the Fellowship? The central focus of the programme is the intersection between advanced AI and biosecurity . This includes exploring how AI could influence biological risks and how technology, research, policy and governance can be used to reduce those risks. The fellowship particularly focuses on reducing global catastrophic biological risks , including potential risks associated with engineered pandemics and biological threats that could be amplified by increasingly capable AI systems. The programme therefore provides an opportunity for fellows to examine questions around how advanced technologies should be developed, governed and deployed in ways that reduce catastrophic risks. Fellowship Tracks The AIxBio Fellowship offers three primary tracks: Research Placement Founding These tracks provide different ways for fellows to contribute to the programme depending on their background, interests and career objectives. Research Track The Research Track is suitable for participants who want to investigate important questions related to AI and biosecurity. Research projects may address topics across areas such as: AI safety Biological AI Biosecurity AI-enabled biological risks Risk assessment Biosecurity safeguards AI governance Biological security Technology policy Global catastrophic biological risks Participants can use the fellowship period to develop and investigate important questions while receiving support and mentorship. The research environment can also provide an opportunity to develop ideas that may lead to future research projects, publications, policy work or other professional activities. Placement Track The Placement Track is designed to provide fellows with practical exposure and opportunities to work on relevant problems in an organisational or professional setting. This track may be particularly attractive to individuals who want to apply their existing technical, research, policy or professional skills to real-world AI-biosecurity challenges. A placement can help participants understand how organisations approach emerging technological and biological risks and how interdisciplinary expertise can be translated into practical solutions. Founding Track The Founding Track is designed for entrepreneurs and individuals interested in building organisations, initiatives or solutions addressing AI-biosecurity problems. This track can be particularly relevant to founders and technically minded individuals who see opportunities to develop new tools, organisations or approaches to reducing biological risks associated with advanced AI. The programme s support can help participants develop their ideas, strengthen their understanding of the problem space and connect with relevant experts and networks. What Does the Fellowship Provide? The AIxBio Fellowship offers a combination of financial support, professional development, expert guidance and networking. £10,000 Total Stipend Selected fellows will receive a £10,000 total stipend for the 10-week programme. This financial support is intended to support fellows while they participate in the full-time programme in Cambridge. Expert Mentorship Fellows will receive expert mentorship throughout the programme. Mentorship can be particularly valuable for participants entering a new interdisciplinary field because it can help them understand the technical, scientific, policy and professional landscape surrounding AI and biosecurity. Research Management The programme provides research management support , which can help fellows structure and execute projects effectively. This is particularly relevant to fellows working on complex questions that require interdisciplinary research and collaboration. Workshops Participants will have access to workshops designed to develop their knowledge and skills. These workshops can provide opportunities to explore emerging issues and learn from experts working in relevant areas.
