title: HM Treasury Government Economic Service Student Placements 2026: Paid Summer and Sandwich Opportunities for Economics Students
summary: The UK Government, through the Government Economic Service (GES) , offers university students an opportunity to gain practical experience in government economics through two student placement routes: the GES Summer Placement Scheme and the GES Sandwich Student Placement Scheme . Both opportunities are designed for students in the penultimate year of an undergraduate degree who are interested in applying economics to real-world public policy challenges. The placements provide exposure to the work of government economists, allowing successful candidates to develop professional skills while contributing to work that supports government decision-making. HM Treasury confirms that the Government Economic Service operates two centrally managed student work-experience schemes: a 6–12-week summer placement and a 12-month sandwich placement . These opportunities can be particularly valuable for students who are considering a future career in economics, public policy, government analysis or the wider Civil Service. 1. HM Treasury Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme The Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme is a paid short-term opportunity for eligible economics undergraduates who want to gain practical experience during the summer. The scheme is intended for students who are considering a future career in the Government Economic Service after completing their studies. According to the current GOV.UK information, the 2026 Summer Placement Scheme is open for applications from 1 October 2026 to 16 October 2026 . What is the Summer Placement Scheme? The summer scheme allows successful students to spend 6 to 12 weeks working within the UK Civil Service during the summer period. Rather than learning economics exclusively through lectures, textbooks and examinations, participants have the opportunity to apply their academic knowledge to practical issues facing government. Students may work in government departments across the United Kingdom, with the exact locations and opportunities varying according to the participating departments and vacancies available during each recruitment round. The experience can provide an important bridge between university study and a professional career in economics. What can students gain from the summer placement? A placement with the Government Economic Service can help students develop an understanding of how economics contributes to public policy. Participants can gain experience in areas such as: Applying economic theory to real-world policy questions Understanding how government departments use economic evidence Conducting economic analysis Supporting policy development Preparing analysis and briefings Working with experienced economists Understanding the Civil Service working environment Developing professional communication skills Building analytical and problem-solving abilities Learning how economic evidence can influence government decisions The experience is particularly useful for students who want to understand how economics works beyond the university classroom. Click HERE for more information 2. HM Treasury Sandwich Student Placement Scheme The second opportunity is the Government Economic Service Sandwich Student Placement Scheme . Unlike the summer scheme, which lasts between six and twelve weeks, the sandwich placement provides an opportunity to spend approximately one year working in government before returning to university to complete an undergraduate degree. The scheme is specifically aimed at economics undergraduates in their penultimate year . Students spend the placement period working alongside experienced government economists and policy professionals before returning to their university studies. A year of practical government experience The sandwich scheme offers students a substantially longer period of professional experience than the summer programme. During the placement, students can experience what it is like to work as part of a government economic team and contribute to policy-related work. The opportunity is designed to connect academic economics with real government decision-making. Students can potentially work on issues that have implications for public policy and society, while developing an understanding of how economic analysis is used within government. The GES describes its sandwich scheme as an opportunity for students to spend a year working in a government department, learning about the role of economics in government and making a contribution to society. Click HERE for more information 3. How the Two Opportunities Compare Although both schemes are part of the Government Economic Service, they are designed around different placement lengths. Feature Summer Placement Scheme Sandwich Student Placement Organisation Government Economic Service Government Economic Service Main institution UK Government/HM Treasury-led GES UK Government/HM Treasury-led GES Duration 6–12 weeks Approximately 12 months Timing Summer One academic placement year Target students Penultimate-year economics undergraduates Penultimate-year economics undergraduates Academic requirement On track for 2:1 or First Penultimate-year economics undergraduate; scheme-specific requirements apply Purpose Short-term professional experience Extended professional placement Paid Yes Yes Location Government departments across the UK Government departments across the UK Main focus Applying economics in practice Applying economics through a longer government placement HM Treasury describes both routes as student work-experience schemes operated through the Government Economic Service. 4. Who Should Consider Applying? These opportunities are particularly relevant to students who are interested in combining economics with public service. They may appeal to students interested in: Economics Public policy Government Public finance Economic development Fiscal policy Monetary and macroeconomic issues Government decision-making Evidence-based policy Public administration Economic research Civil Service careers For students considering a career as a government economist, the schemes can provide an opportunity to understand the profession before graduation. The Government Economic Service also offers other routes into government economics, including graduate-level opportunities such as the Assistant Economist Scheme and Government Economic Service Fast Stream . 5. Summer Placement Eligibility Requirements The Summer Placement Scheme has specific academic requirements. According to the current GOV.UK guidance, applicants must be in the penultimate year of undergraduate study . This means that after completing the placement, the student must have one further year of university study remaining before completing their undergraduate degree. Applicants must also be on track to achieve at least a 2:1 or First Class degree , based on their results so far. Importantly, the economics requirement is specific. Applicants must be studying one of the following: An undergraduate degree in Economics, either BA or BSc; An undergraduate joint degree containing Economics, where Economics represents at least 50% of the credit value of the modules studied and to be studied throughout the degree; or An undergraduate Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) honours degree where Economics represents at least 50% of the relevant credit value . Applicants must also have studied both microeconomics and macroeconomics . Candidates must additionally satisfy the relevant UK immigration requirements and the Civil Service Nationality Rules . The Government Economic Service states that it does not provide visa sponsorship for these schemes. 6. Sandwich Placement Eligibility The Sandwich Student Placement is also aimed at students in their penultimate year of undergraduate study . The purpose of the placement is for students to spend a year working in government and then return to university to complete their degree. This means applicants should not be students who are already completing their final year. The GES describes its student schemes as routes specifically designed for students in their penultimate year of study. As with the Summer Scheme, applicants must meet the applicable immigration and Civil Service nationality requirements, and the GES does not provide sponsorship for these schemes. Because eligibility conditions can differ between recruitment rounds and individual schemes, applicants should carefully review the official requirements before submitting an application. 7. Where Can Successful Students Work? The opportunities are not necessarily restricted to HM Treasury itself. The Government Economic Service supports economic work across different UK government departments. Civil Service information identifies organisations and departments where GES economists can work, including HM Treasury, HM Revenue Customs, the Office for National Statistics, the Home Office and the Ministry of Justice. The exact department and location available to a student can vary from one recruitment year to another. The Summer Scheme guidance specifically states that opportunities are available in a range of government departments across the UK and that locations vary according to the department and year. This means successful students may gain exposure to economic issues within different areas of government rather than working exclusively on one type of economic policy. Click HERE for more information 8. Why This Experience Matters One of the strongest features of these programmes is the opportunity to move from academic economics to practical economics . At university, students may study economic models, theories, statistics, microeconomics and macroeconomics. A government placement provides an opportunity to see how this knowledge can be applied to real policy questions. For example, economic analysis can help governments think about: Public spending Taxation Economic growth Employment Government programmes Public services Investment Business and economic development The impact of policy decisions on households and businesses Working within government can therefore help students understand the relationship between economic evidence, political priorities and public policy. 9. Professional Development A placement can also help students develop skills that are valuable beyond economics. These may include: Analytical skills Students can develop their ability to analyse information, interpret evidence and approach complex problems systematically. Communication skills Government economists need to communicate technical economic information clearly to policymakers and other audiences. Policy understanding Students can learn how evidence is incorporated into the policy-making process. Teamwork Working within a government department gives students experience collaborating with economists, civil servants, policy professionals and other specialists. Professional experience The placement provides experience within the Civil Service, helping students understand professional standards, organisational structures and government working environments. Career exploration The experience can also help students decide whether government economics is the right career path for them. 10. A Potential Pathway into a Government Economics Career For students who want to become government economists, these programmes can form part of a broader career pathway. The Government Economic Service operates several recruitment routes covering different stages of a person s career. These include student schemes, graduate opportunities and other routes into the economics profession. A student could therefore use a placement to gain practical experience and then explore graduate opportunities within the Government Economic Service after completing their degree. The GES also has a Fast Stream and Assistant Economist Scheme for graduates. 11. Application Deadline Summer Placement Scheme For the 2026 Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme , applications are open from: 1 October 2026 to 16 October 2026. Therefore, prospective applicants should ensure that they complete their application before 16 October 2026 . CLICK HERE TO APPLY FOR SUMMER PLACEMENT SCHEME Sandwich Student Placement Scheme The information provided for the Sandwich Student Placement Scheme does not state a specific application deadline . The GES describes the Sandwich Scheme as an annual student recruitment route that opens in the autumn. CLICH HERE TO APPLY FOR THE SANDWICH STUDENT PLACEMENT SCHEME Applicants should therefore check the official GES recruitment page for the current recruitment timetable and closing date before applying. 12. Important Information for International Students International applicants should pay particular attention to the nationality and immigration requirements. Although the schemes are advertised internationally and may be of interest to students studying outside the UK, eligibility is not determined simply by being an undergraduate student. Candidates must meet the relevant Civil Service Nationality Rules and immigration requirements. The GES explicitly states that it does not offer visa sponsorship for these schemes. Therefore, students who do not already have the necessary right to work in the UK should carefully examine the nationality and immigration requirements before investing time in an application. 13. Why Students Should Consider the Opportunity The HM Treasury/Government Economic Service student schemes offer a combination of paid professional experience, exposure to government and practical application of economics . For an eligible economics student, the opportunity can provide: Real-world government experience Paid employment during the placement Exposure to experienced economists Experience applying economics to policy Professional networking Development of analytical and communication skills Understanding of Civil Service careers Exposure to government departments An opportunity to explore a long-term career in public-sector economics The longer sandwich placement can be particularly valuable for students seeking substantial professional experience before graduating, while the summer scheme provides a shorter route for students who want to gain government experience without taking an entire year away from their studies. 14. Conclusion The HM Treasury Government Economic Service Summer Placement Scheme and Sandwich Student Placement Scheme provide opportunities for eligible undergraduate economics students to experience how economics is applied within the UK Government. The Summer Placement Scheme offers a paid 6–12-week experience during the summer, while the Sandwich Student Placement Scheme provides an opportunity to spend approximately one year working in government before returning to university . Both schemes are designed to help students move beyond theoretical learning and understand how economic analysis contributes to real-world government decisions. For the 2026 Summer Scheme, applications are open from 1 October to 16 October 2026 , making the deadline particularly important for eligible students who wish to apply this year. Students interested in a future career in government economics, public policy or the Civil Service should examine the eligibility criteria carefully and use the official Government Economic Service recruitment information when preparing their applications. Who Can Apply? Summer Placement Scheme The primary eligible applicants are: Undergraduate students in their penultimate year . Students on track for a 2:1 or First Class degree . Students studying Economics , an Economics joint degree with Economics comprising at least 50% of credits, or qualifying PPE degrees with Economics comprising at least 50%. Applicants must have studied both microeconomics and macroeconomics . Applicants must satisfy the relevant UK immigration and Civil Service Nationality Rules. Sandwich Student Placement Scheme The scheme is aimed at: Undergraduate students in their penultimate year . Students who will return to university after the placement to complete their degree. Economics undergraduates meeting the specific GES requirements. Applicants who satisfy the relevant UK immigration and Civil Service Nationality Rules. Official Application Information For more information on the government service summer scheme, click HERE For more information on HM Treasury recruitment, click HERE Nationality / Countries / Continent There is no simple “open to all countries” rule for these schemes. Eligibility is governed by the UK Civil Service Nationality Rules and immigration requirements . The GES states that it does not provide visa sponsorship for these student schemes. Therefore, applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas or other regions should not assume that nationality alone makes them eligible. They must establish that they have the required nationality/immigration status and right to work under the applicable UK rules. title: Smithsonian Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027: Fully Funded Postdoctoral Research Opportunity in Systematic Ichthyology
summary: The Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology 2027 is offering an exceptional research opportunity for qualified early-career researchers seeking to undertake advanced, collections-based research on fish systematics at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History (NMNH) in the United States. Supported through an endowed fellowship established by Bruce B. Collette and his wife, Sara, the programme is designed to support the next generation of researchers working in systematic ichthyology , particularly research involving comparative morphology and the study of fish collections. The fellowship provides an opportunity for a postdoctoral researcher to conduct full-time, resident and independent research using the Smithsonian s extensive fish collections, scientific facilities, library resources and expertise. The award is for one year , with the possibility of renewal. Applications are open to both US and non-US citizens , making this a significant international postdoctoral opportunity for qualified researchers from around the world. Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at the Smithsonian The fellowship was established in 2017 through the generous support of Bruce B. Collette , whose scientific career has focused extensively on collections-based systematic studies of marine fishes. Dr. Collette began his career in 1960 and spent nearly six decades within the National Museum of Natural History community through his work with the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) and NOAA , as well as through his affiliation with the Smithsonian. His longstanding connection to the museum s collections, library and scientific community inspired the creation of this fellowship. The fellowship is intended to provide emerging researchers with an opportunity to experience and use the Smithsonian s scientific collections and resources while contributing to the field of collections-based ichthyology. The fellowship therefore combines advanced independent research, access to world-class scientific collections, mentorship and participation in a broader international research community . Purpose of the Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship The central purpose of the fellowship is to support full-time, resident, independent postdoctoral research in systematics , including comparative morphology, with a particular emphasis on using the fish collections held by the National Museum of Natural History. The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers whose work can benefit substantially from the Smithsonian s extensive collections and specialized research infrastructure. Awardees are expected to become actively involved in the scholarly activities of the Division of Fishes and contribute to the broader field of collections-based systematic ichthyology at both national and international levels. This means that the fellowship is not simply intended to provide financial support for independent research. It is designed to integrate fellows into a major scientific research environment where they can interact with researchers, collections specialists, curators and other members of the scientific community. What Does the Fellowship Focus On? The fellowship focuses on systematic ichthyology , the scientific study of fish diversity, classification, evolutionary relationships and related areas. Research may involve areas such as: Fish systematics Comparative morphology Taxonomic revisions Phylogeny Higher classification Biogeography Fish evolution Osteology Myology Reproductive morphology Larval fish studies Ontogeny Collections-based research Comparative studies of fish specimens Priority is given to proposals that clearly demonstrate how the researcher will use the Smithsonian s fish collection and other resources to advance their research. Research Opportunities at the Division of Fishes The Smithsonian s Division of Fishes provides an extensive scientific environment for researchers interested in fish systematics and related disciplines. Current research activities include systematic revisions of species, genera and families, as well as research into higher classification and biogeography. Research efforts have included work on: Caribbean marine shorefish Indo-Pacific marine shorefish Beloniform fishes Scombroid fishes Pleuronectiform fishes Tetraodontiform fishes Larval fishes Fish ontogeny Reproductive morphology Southeast Asian freshwater fishes Phylogeny and higher classification Researchers also have access to osteological, myological and other comparative studies that support the investigation of evolutionary relationships across a broad range of fish taxa. Access to One of the World s Largest Fish Collections One of the major advantages of the Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship is access to the Smithsonian s extensive Division of Fishes collection . The collection contains more than 975,000 lots , representing more than 6 million individual fish specimens . A lot refers to specimens of the same species collected at the same time and place. The collection is organized phylogenetically by family and alphabetically by genus and species within each family. More than half of the collection has been computer catalogued and is available through an online searchable database. The collection has particularly strong holdings of: North American fishes Neotropical fishes Caribbean fishes West Pacific fishes This makes the fellowship particularly valuable for researchers whose projects require extensive comparative specimen-based research. Additional Scientific Resources Beyond the fish specimens themselves, fellows will have access to additional scientific resources that can support sophisticated research projects. These resources include: Illustrations and photographs of fishes Radiographs MicroCT facilities Molecular laboratory facilities Scanning electron microscopes Digital imaging facilities Radiographic systems Light photography systems Specialized research equipment A dedicated fish research library Extensive scientific reprints Archives containing original illustrations, maps and photographs The fish collection includes approximately 25,000 units of illustrations and photographs and approximately 25,000 radiographs . The Division of Fishes library contains more than 8,000 volumes , together with an extensive collection of reprints and archives. These resources can provide researchers with opportunities to conduct research that may not be possible using their home institution s resources alone. Fellowship Duration The Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship is a one-year award . The fellowship may be renewed, subject to the applicable conditions and review processes. For the 2027 fellowship cycle, the eligible start-date window is: Earliest start date: February 2, 2027 Latest start date: June 7, 2027 All formal requirements for the PhD must have been completed before the fellowship begins . Fellowship Location The fellowship is an in-person residential research opportunity . The primary locations are: National Museum of Natural History, Washington, DC and Museum Support Center, Suitland, Maryland Because the fellowship is designed around direct access to the Smithsonian s collections, laboratories, library and research community, applicants should be prepared to undertake their fellowship in person. Financial Benefits and Award Package The Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship provides a substantial financial package to support the fellow throughout the one-year research period. The standard one-year award package includes: $65,000 Annual Stipend The fellow will receive a $65,000 annual stipend . This provides the principal financial support for the one-year fellowship period. $5,000 Research and Travel Allowance The fellowship provides an additional $5,000 research/travel allowance . This can support eligible research-related expenses and travel associated with the fellowship. Applicants are encouraged to consider scientific meetings and opportunities to promote collections-based research when developing their research plans and budgets. $5,000 Health Insurance Allowance The fellowship includes a $5,000 health insurance allowance . This contributes to eligible health insurance costs during the fellowship. $1,000 Relocation Allowance The award also includes a one-time $1,000 relocation allowance . This is particularly relevant to fellows who need to relocate to the Washington, DC, or Suitland, Maryland, area for the fellowship. Total Fellowship Package The stated one-year award package totals $75,000 , with an additional $1,000 in the first year for relocation , meaning the first-year financial package can amount to $76,000 when the relocation allowance is included . Applicants should review the official fellowship terms carefully when preparing their financial plans. Who Is Eligible for the Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship? The fellowship is open to both US and non-US citizens . Applicants should have a demonstrated record of research achievement and knowledge of the systematics of one or more groups of fishes. In addition, applicants must have completed all formal requirements for their PhD before the start of the fellowship tenure . The fellowship is therefore aimed at researchers who have already completed doctoral-level training and are ready to undertake independent postdoctoral research. Key Eligibility Requirements Applicants should: Be a US or non-US citizen. Hold a PhD or have completed all formal PhD requirements before the fellowship begins. Have a demonstrated record of research accomplishment. Have knowledge of the systematics of one or more groups of fishes. Be prepared to conduct full-time, resident research. Have a research project appropriate for the fellowship. Be able to make meaningful use of the Smithsonian s fish collections and associated research resources. Priority Will Be Given to Strong Research Proposals Although the fellowship is open to eligible applicants internationally, the Smithsonian has identified particular characteristics that will receive priority during consideration. Priority will be given to proposals that: Focus on systematic ichthyology Research should have a strong connection to systematic ichthyology and related areas of fish systematics. Demonstrate high research productivity and creativity Applicants should demonstrate their ability to conduct high-quality research and contribute innovative ideas to their field. Demonstrate strong potential for interaction The proposed work should show potential for scholarly interaction and engagement within the Division of Fishes and the broader research community. Make meaningful use of Smithsonian collections Applicants should clearly explain why the Smithsonian s fish collections and other NMNH resources are important to their research. The last point is particularly important. Applicants should not simply propose a project that could be conducted anywhere. The proposal should demonstrate why conducting the research at the Smithsonian is scientifically valuable. Application Materials Applicants must submit their applications through the Smithsonian s Online Application System (SOLAA) . The application must include several important components. 1. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a CV containing relevant information such as: Education Areas of expertise Research achievements Honors Publications Research interests The CV should provide a clear picture of the applicant s research background and academic accomplishments. 2. Recent Publications Applicants may submit a maximum of three PDF publications . These publications should help demonstrate the applicant s research productivity, expertise and ability to contribute to the proposed area of study. 3. Research Proposal Applicants must provide a research proposal consisting of: Abstract Research statement Timetable Budget The research proposal is one of the most important components of the application because it enables reviewers to assess the scientific value, feasibility and relevance of the proposed research. 4. Two Letters of Reference Applicants must arrange for two letters of reference . The referees should be individuals who are familiar with the applicant s work. The referees are expected to submit their letters separately through the online application system. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that the letters are submitted by the deadline. Research Proposal Requirements The research proposal must be carefully structured and address the specific requirements outlined by the Smithsonian. Abstract The proposal must include an abstract of the proposed research. The abstract is limited to 250 words . Applicants should use the abstract to clearly communicate the research question, approach and significance of the proposed project. Full Research Proposal The full research statement should describe the research planned for the one-year fellowship. It should address: Research methodology Importance of the research Relevance to the broader discipline Importance of the research to the applicant s scholarly development Reasons for conducting the research at the Smithsonian How the applicant will use resources in the Department of Vertebrate Zoology and Division of Fishes The research proposal is limited to three double-spaced pages , including figures, using 11-point type . Timetable Applicants must provide a detailed timetable showing how they intend to accomplish their research objectives during the one-year fellowship. The timetable should include: Major research milestones Expected stages of the project Estimated travel dates Important activities required to complete the research A realistic timetable can demonstrate that the proposed project is achievable within the fellowship period. Budget and Justification Applicants must provide a detailed budget and justification covering items such as: Equipment Supplies Research-related travel Other research support The budget should exclude the stipend and relocation costs . Applicants are strongly encouraged to consider including travel to scientific meetings and activities that promote collections-based research. Where possible, applicants are also encouraged to discuss anticipated research expenses with NMNH staff before submitting their application. If the proposed research requires funding beyond the $5,000 annual research allowance , applicants should explain where the additional funding would come from. Bibliography Applicants should provide a bibliography of literature relevant to their proposed research where necessary. The bibliography is limited to two pages . References Applicants must provide the names and email addresses of the two individuals who will submit letters of reference. Applicants are encouraged to provide their referees with a copy of the research proposal so that the references can be prepared appropriately. Applicants should also follow up with referees to ensure that their letters are submitted before the application deadline. Identifying an Advisor A particularly important component of the application is identifying an appropriate fellowship advisor. Applicants must identify: One member of the NMNH Fish Division staff or affiliated staff, including retirees , to serve as their principal fellowship advisor. A second person to serve as an alternate or co-advisor. This means prospective applicants should carefully examine the research interests and expertise of Smithsonian Fish Division personnel and identify researchers whose expertise aligns with their proposed project. Establishing this alignment can help applicants demonstrate that their project fits within the scientific environment and resources of the Smithsonian. How to Apply for the Smithsonian Collette Fellowship Applications must be submitted through the Smithsonian s SOLAA online application system . Applicants should follow these steps: Step 1: Create an Account or Log In Applicants should create a SOLAA account or log into an existing account. Step 2: Start the Application After logging in, select the option to Start Application . Step 3: Select the Institution Select: NMNH – National Museum of Natural History as the Office/Museum/Research Center. Step 4: Search for the Fellowship Search for: Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology Step 5: Select Apply Now Once the programme is located, select Apply Now and proceed with the application. Applicants should ensure that all required documents are uploaded and that reference letters are submitted before the closing deadline. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The application deadline for the Sara E. and Bruce B. Collette Postdoctoral Fellowship in Systematic Ichthyology is: November 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST. Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications because they need to allow sufficient time for uploading documents and ensuring that their two referees submit their recommendation letters. Access to Exceptional Scientific Collections Researchers gain access to one of the world s largest comparative fish collections, containing millions of individual specimens. International Research Environment The fellowship brings researchers into the Smithsonian s international scientific community and provides opportunities for scholarly interaction. Advanced Research Infrastructure Access to specialized equipment and facilities can support sophisticated research methodologies. Professional Development Participation in the Division of Fishes can help fellows expand their professional networks and develop relationships with researchers in their field. Independent Research The programme is designed around independent postdoctoral research, allowing fellows to develop and execute a substantial research project. Potential Career Development The careers of previous fellows demonstrate how specialized postdoctoral training and access to major natural history collections can contribute to future academic and museum-based careers. Explain specifically why the NMNH Division of Fishes collection is necessary or particularly valuable for the proposed work. title: Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026: Apply for a Youth Policy, Governance and Advocacy Training Programme in Kaduna State
summary: The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is inviting young people in Kaduna State, Nigeria, who are passionate about governance, public policy, accountability and social change to apply for a practical training and mentorship programme designed to develop the next generation of youth policy analysts. The programme will equip selected participants with practical skills in policy analysis, policy research, policy writing, budget literacy and evidence-based advocacy . Participants will also have an opportunity to work collaboratively with other young people, develop policy briefs and engage with government institutions on governance and public policy issues. With only 25 participants set to be selected, the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 offers a focused opportunity for young people who want to better understand how policy decisions are made and how evidence, data and technology can be used to promote accountable governance and meaningful social change. About the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is designed as a practical learning and engagement programme for young people interested in the intersection of youth participation, governance, public policy, data, accountability and community development . Rather than focusing solely on theoretical learning, the programme is structured around practical activities that can help participants understand how policy research and advocacy work in real-world settings. Participants will take part in a two-day non-residential policy bootcamp , receive mentorship, collaborate in teams and work towards producing policy briefs addressing governance and policy challenges relevant to Kaduna State. The programme also includes opportunities for participants to participate in advocacy engagements with government institutions , giving young people exposure to how policy discussions can connect with public institutions and decision-makers. What Will Participants Gain? Selected participants will have the opportunity to develop a range of practical skills and experiences relevant to careers in public policy, governance, research, advocacy, development and civic engagement. 1. Two-Day Policy Bootcamp Participants will participate in an intensive two-day policy bootcamp designed to strengthen their understanding of policy-related issues and provide practical learning opportunities. The bootcamp is expected to provide a collaborative environment where young people can learn, exchange ideas and apply policy concepts to real governance challenges. 2. Policy Research and Analysis Skills The programme will help participants strengthen their ability to conduct policy research and analyse governance-related issues. These skills can be particularly valuable for young people interested in careers or further studies involving: Public policy Governance Development Political science International development Research Advocacy Public administration Civil society Government and public institutions 3. Policy Writing Experience Participants will gain practical exposure to policy writing , including working with other participants to develop policy briefs. A policy brief is an important tool for communicating research and evidence to policymakers and other stakeholders. Learning how to identify a policy problem, examine evidence and formulate practical recommendations can therefore be valuable for anyone interested in influencing public policy. 4. Mentorship The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab will provide participants with mentorship opportunities , allowing them to learn from individuals with relevant knowledge and experience. Mentorship can help young participants better understand policy careers, advocacy, research and approaches to addressing governance challenges. 5. Teamwork and Collaboration Participants will work with other young people during the programme, including collaborating on policy briefs. This will provide an opportunity to strengthen skills such as Teamwork Communication Problem-solving Research collaboration Leadership Critical thinking Stakeholder engagement 6. Advocacy Engagements Participants will have the opportunity to take part in advocacy engagements with government institutions . This component can give young people practical exposure to government engagement and demonstrate how evidence and policy recommendations can be communicated to public institutions. 7. Understanding of Budget Literacy and Accountability The programme specifically seeks to build skills around budget literacy and accountable governance. Understanding public budgets is important because government budgets influence the resources available for public services, development programmes and community priorities. Young people who develop budget literacy can become better equipped to examine public expenditure, ask informed questions and participate constructively in discussions about government accountability. Policy Issues Participants Can Explore Applicants are asked to indicate the governance or policy issue that interests them most. The available areas include: Youth Employment and Economic Opportunities Youth employment is an important policy issue, particularly in relation to access to decent work, entrepreneurship, skills development and economic opportunities. Participants interested in this area may explore policies affecting young people s participation in the economy and potential approaches to expanding employment and livelihood opportunities. Education Financing and Accountability Education financing and accountability focus on how resources are allocated to education and how stakeholders can promote transparency and effective use of public resources. This area may appeal to applicants interested in education policy, public finance, access to education and accountability. Public Expenditure and Budget Transparency This area focuses on understanding how public resources are allocated and spent. Applicants interested in public financial management can use the programme as an opportunity to develop their understanding of budgets, expenditure and transparency. Local Government Accountability and Service Delivery Local governments play an important role in delivering services and responding to community needs. Participants interested in this area may explore how local government institutions can improve accountability, responsiveness and service delivery. AI Governance and Data-Driven Public Policy The programme also highlights the growing importance of Artificial Intelligence and data-driven tools in policy analysis and governance . Applicants are specifically asked to explain how AI and data-driven tools can contribute to policy analysis, good governance and social change in Kaduna State. This makes the programme particularly relevant to young people interested in the intersection of technology, artificial intelligence, data and public policy . Who Can Apply? The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is intended for young people residing in Kaduna State, Nigeria , particularly those who have an interest in governance, public policy and creating positive change in their communities. Applicants should demonstrate an interest in issues such as governance, policy, accountability, research, advocacy, leadership or social change. The application form asks applicants to provide information including: Full name Email address Age Gender Residence within Kaduna City Current occupation Institution or organization Previous experience Policy interests Motivation for joining the programme Expected learning outcomes Availability for the two-day bootcamp Willingness to work in a team Willingness to participate in a government advocacy visit Accessibility support requirements The programme will select only 25 participants , making it important for applicants to complete the application carefully and provide clear, thoughtful responses. Previous Experience Is Not the Only Consideration The application asks whether applicants have previous experience in community engagement, advocacy, research or leadership . Applicants who answer yes are asked to briefly describe their experience. However, the application also allows applicants to indicate that they do not have previous experience. This means applicants should carefully answer the question honestly rather than assuming that they need extensive professional experience to apply. Young people who have participated in community activities, student leadership, volunteer initiatives, research projects, advocacy campaigns or other forms of civic engagement may wish to explain these experiences clearly. AI, Data and the Future of Public Policy One of the distinctive elements of the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is its emphasis on Artificial Intelligence and data-driven tools . Applicants are asked how AI and data-driven tools can contribute to policy analysis, good governance and social change in Kaduna State. This question gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate their understanding of how technology can support evidence-based decision-making. For example, AI and data tools can potentially support policy work by helping stakeholders: Analyse large volumes of information. Identify trends and patterns in datasets. Support evidence-based research. Improve access to information. Identify emerging social and economic issues. Support monitoring and evaluation. Improve public service planning. Strengthen data-informed decision-making. However, responsible use of AI also requires attention to issues such as data privacy, accuracy, bias, transparency, accountability and human oversight. Applicants may therefore want to demonstrate a balanced understanding of both the opportunities and responsibilities associated with using AI in public policy. Application Questions Applicants will be required to respond to a series of questions designed to assess their background, interests, motivation and availability. Some of the key questions include: Why do you want to join the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026? How do you think AI and data-driven tools can contribute to policy analysis, good governance and social change in Kaduna State? Which governance or policy issue interests you most? Do you have previous experience in community engagement, advocacy, research or leadership? What do you hope to learn from the programme? Are you available to participate in the two-day non-residential bootcamp? Are you willing to work with a team to develop a policy brief? Are you willing to participate in a government advocacy visit? Do you require any accessibility support to participate? Applicants should take time to provide thoughtful and specific responses rather than submitting generic statements. How to Strengthen Your Application Because only 25 participants will be selected , applicants should make their responses as relevant and compelling as possible. Demonstrate Your Interest in Governance Explain what attracts you to governance and public policy and, where possible, connect your interest to a specific issue affecting communities in Kaduna State. Be Specific About Your Motivation Instead of simply stating that you want to gain experience, explain what you hope to learn and how you intend to use those skills after completing the programme. Highlight Relevant Experience If you have participated in research, student leadership, community initiatives, volunteering, advocacy, civic activities or other projects, briefly explain what you did and what you learned. Connect Technology to Policy Since the application specifically asks about AI and data-driven tools, applicants should demonstrate an understanding of how technology can support evidence-based policymaking while acknowledging the importance of responsible and ethical use. Demonstrate Your Willingness to Collaborate The programme involves teamwork and development of policy briefs. Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they are comfortable working with people who may have different perspectives and experiences. Show Your Interest in Practical Impact Strong applicants can explain how they would use the knowledge gained from the programme to contribute to their community, professional development or future policy and advocacy work. Programme Participation Requirements Applicants should carefully consider the practical participation requirements before applying. Selected participants are expected to: Be available for the two-day non-residential bootcamp. Work collaboratively with other participants. Contribute to the development of a policy brief. Participate in relevant advocacy activities. Be willing to engage with government institutions as part of the programme. Provide complete and accurate information in the application form. Applicants can also indicate whether they require accessibility support to participate. Number of Participants The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 is a selective programme. Only 25 participants will be selected. This limited cohort is likely to allow for a more focused learning environment, closer collaboration among participants and practical engagement around policy issues. Application Deadline Deadline: Not specified in the information provided. Applicants should therefore check the official application form or programme announcement for any deadline or closing date before submitting their application. APPLY HERE How to Apply Interested young people should complete the online application form and provide all the required information. The application form is hosted on Google Forms and asks applicants to provide personal information, educational or occupational details, their policy interests, relevant experience, motivation and availability. Applicants should carefully review all responses before submitting because the programme states that only 25 participants will be selected. Visit HERE for more information about the Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026. Conclusion The Kaduna Youth Policy Lab 2026 presents an opportunity for young people in Kaduna State to strengthen their understanding of public policy, governance, accountability and evidence-based advocacy while developing practical research and policy-writing skills. Through the two-day policy bootcamp, mentorship, teamwork, policy brief development and government advocacy engagements, participants will have the opportunity to move beyond theoretical discussions and gain practical exposure to policy processes. The programme s focus on AI, data-driven policy analysis, budget literacy, public expenditure, local government accountability, education financing and youth economic opportunities also makes it particularly relevant to young people interested in the future of governance and evidence-based decision-making. With only 25 participants to be selected , eligible young people who are passionate about improving governance and creating positive change in their communities should prepare their applications carefully and clearly demonstrate their motivation, policy interests, relevant experiences and commitment to participating in the full programme. For more global Training opportunities, visit OFY HERE. title: 71st and 72nd IATSS Forum 2027: 8-Week Leadership Development Programme in Japan for Professionals from Asia
summary: The IATSS Forum 2027 is inviting applications from young professionals and emerging leaders who are interested in developing their leadership capabilities, exchanging knowledge across cultures and contributing to sustainable development in their countries and the wider Asian region. The programme is designed around the idea of co-creative and collaborative leadership , bringing together professionals from different countries, cultures, professional backgrounds and areas of expertise. Participants are expected not only to learn from the programme but also to share their own experiences, knowledge, perspectives and professional expertise with other participants. For 2027, the programme will be conducted through two possible eight-week sessions: the 71st IATSS Forum from May to July 2027 and the 72nd IATSS Forum from September to November 2027 . Applicants should note that the programme schedule and timeframe may be subject to change, and applicants cannot guarantee or select which programme period they will ultimately be assigned to. The IATSS Forum is particularly interested in individuals who have demonstrated leadership experience, understand the challenges facing their communities and countries, possess a strong desire to create positive change, and have the potential to use the knowledge and networks gained through the programme for the benefit of society. IATSS Forum 2027 Programme Overview The IATSS Forum is structured as an intensive international learning and leadership development experience. It provides participants with an opportunity to step outside their usual professional and cultural environments and engage with people from different backgrounds. The programme places particular importance on: Leadership development Cross-cultural understanding Collaborative and co-creative leadership Sustainable regional development Knowledge and experience sharing Professional and personal development Understanding social and regional challenges Building international networks Learning from people with different professional and cultural perspectives Developing the ability to contribute to communities and society Participants are expected to actively engage in lectures, group discussions, meetings, learning activities, and other programme components. The programme is therefore intended for individuals who are not simply looking to attend an international programme, but who have a clear idea of how the experience can contribute to their future leadership journey and their ability to create positive change. IATSS Forum 2027 Programme Dates The 2027 programme is currently scheduled across two possible eight-week periods. 71st IATSS Forum May to July 2027 Duration: 8 weeks 72nd IATSS Forum September to November 2027 Duration: 8 weeks Applicants should be aware that the programme schedule and timeframe are subject to change . In addition, applicants cannot guarantee which of the two programme periods they will be assigned to. Selection for the programme therefore does not necessarily mean that an applicant will be able to choose between the May–July and September–November sessions. Application Deadline for IATSS Forum 2027 The application period for the 2027 IATSS Forum runs from: 1 June 2026 to 30 September 2026 Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing their documents well before the deadline. The application requires several documents, including an application form, basic question form, essay, recommendation form, and, where applicable, proof of English proficiency. Because some documents may require coordination with an employer or direct supervisor, applicants should avoid waiting until the final days of the application period. Applications must be submitted through the designated online application process. Submissions by email are not accepted. Who Is the IATSS Forum Looking For? The IATSS Forum has outlined several characteristics that it considers important when selecting candidates. The selection process is not based solely on academic qualifications or professional experience. Instead, the programme seeks individuals who demonstrate leadership potential, awareness of social and community issues, a willingness to learn from others, and a clear motivation to contribute to sustainable development. The ideal candidate should be able to demonstrate several of the following qualities. Leadership Experience and Potential Leadership is one of the central qualities sought by the IATSS Forum. Candidates should ideally have experience leading a team within an organisation or professional environment. However, leadership is not presented simply as holding a formal managerial position. The programme is interested in individuals who understand their own leadership strengths as well as the areas where they need to improve. Applicants should therefore be able to reflect on questions such as: What type of leader am I? What leadership responsibilities have I undertaken? What have I learned from leading others? What challenges have I encountered as a leader? What areas of my leadership skills still need development? How do I work with people who have different perspectives from my own? The IATSS Forum places particular emphasis on co-creative and collaborative leadership . This means that effective leadership is understood as the ability to bring together people with different experiences, cultures, professional backgrounds, and perspectives and work collectively towards a shared objective. Candidates should therefore demonstrate an ability and willingness to collaborate rather than relying solely on individual leadership. Co-Creative and Collaborative Leadership A major focus of the IATSS Forum is the concept of co-creative/collaborative leadership . Participants will come from different cultural and professional environments. This diversity is viewed as an opportunity for learning and collective problem-solving. Candidates should understand that leadership can involve: Listening to different perspectives Respecting cultural differences Building consensus Encouraging participation Recognizing the strengths of team members Combining different areas of expertise Working towards common goals Learning from people with different experiences Creating solutions collectively The programme therefore seeks people who can contribute to a diverse learning environment while also learning from others. Awareness of Issues Facing Their Country and Community Another important characteristic is awareness of the challenges facing the applicant s own country and community. Candidates should have an understanding of important social, economic, environmental, institutional, developmental, or other challenges relevant to their communities. However, awareness alone is not sufficient. The IATSS Forum is looking for people who have the motivation to take on a leadership role in addressing these challenges . Applicants should be able to demonstrate that they are not merely observers of problems but are interested in becoming part of the process of creating solutions. This could involve professional work, community engagement, social initiatives, organisational leadership, public policy, development work, business, education, civil society, or other forms of contribution. Commitment to Sustainable Development The programme seeks candidates who are motivated to contribute to the future sustainable development of the region . Applicants should therefore consider how their professional work and leadership can contribute to long-term positive change. This can include developing solutions to challenges affecting communities, improving institutions, supporting inclusive development, strengthening cooperation, or using professional expertise to address problems facing society. Candidates should have a clear understanding of why sustainable development matters to their country and region and how they hope to contribute. Broad Skills, Experience and Expertise The IATSS Forum brings together participants with different professional backgrounds and areas of expertise. Candidates are therefore expected to possess a broad range of skills, experience, and professional knowledge that can be shared with other participants. Applicants should consider what unique perspectives they can bring to the programme. This could include expertise gained through: Professional employment Leadership responsibilities Community initiatives Policy work Research Business Civil society Development programmes Education Public administration Social entrepreneurship Technology Environmental initiatives International cooperation Other professional or community-based activities The important point is that participants should be able to contribute knowledge and experience to discussions and group learning. Strong English Communication Skills English proficiency is an important requirement because the programme involves active participation in an international environment. Candidates should have sufficient English skills to participate effectively in: Lectures Group discussions Meetings Knowledge-sharing sessions Collaborative activities Cross-cultural exchanges Participants are expected not simply to understand English but to be able to communicate their experiences, knowledge, opinions, and ideas to people from different backgrounds. Applicants may submit a certificate demonstrating English proficiency, where applicable. Accepted examples listed in the application information include certificates such as: TOEFL TOEIC Other relevant English proficiency certificates An English proficiency certificate should be attached if applicable. Potential for Personal and Professional Development The IATSS Forum recognises that strong candidates may not already possess every skill required to achieve their long-term goals. The programme is therefore also interested in candidates who have the potential to gain what they currently lack through participation. Applicants should be able to identify areas where they want to grow. For example, a candidate may want to improve: Leadership abilities Cross-cultural communication Collaborative problem-solving Strategic thinking International networking Professional communication Understanding of regional issues Team management Intercultural collaboration Ability to develop sustainable solutions The key is demonstrating how participation in the IATSS Forum can help the applicant become a more effective professional and leader. Independence and Adaptability The programme takes place in a diversified international environment. Candidates should therefore be disciplined, independent, adaptable, and comfortable learning alongside people with different cultural and professional backgrounds. Applicants should demonstrate: Independence Responsibility Adaptability Respect for different cultures Openness to learning Positive engagement with others Willingness to work in diverse teams Participants should also possess the physical and mental capabilities necessary to fully participate in programme activities without an accompanying person. Respect for Diversity and Other Perspectives The IATSS Forum is built around interaction among people from different backgrounds. Candidates should therefore demonstrate a positive attitude towards learning from and respecting others. This means being willing to encounter perspectives that may differ significantly from one s own. Successful participants are expected to: Listen actively Respect different viewpoints Engage constructively in discussions Avoid dismissing unfamiliar perspectives Learn from cultural differences Share their own experiences respectfully Work collaboratively with people from different backgrounds This intercultural dimension is an important part of the programme experience. Clear Goals for Participating in the IATSS Forum Applicants should be able to clearly explain what they hope to gain from participating in the programme. A strong application should therefore connect the applicants: Current experience → Leadership goals → Learning needs → IATSS Forum experience → Future contribution Candidates should have a clear understanding of why the programme is relevant to their professional and personal development. They should also demonstrate that their goals are aligned with the contents and philosophy of the IATSS Forum. IATSS Forum 2027 Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet the programme s eligibility requirements. Nationality Applicants must possess the nationality of one of the following countries: Cambodia India Indonesia Laos Malaysia Myanmar Philippines Singapore Thailand Vietnam Age Applicants must be 35 years old or younger as of the application closing date . Since the application deadline is 30 September 2026 , applicants must meet the age requirement as of that date. Current Employment Applicants must currently be working as a full-time employee in a professional field . The eligibility information also states that: Self-employed applicants can apply. Freelancers can apply. Therefore, the requirement is focused on current professional engagement rather than exclusively requiring employment by a traditional organisation. Professional Experience Applicants should have at least two years of full-time professional job experience at the time of application . Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate meaningful professional experience and explain how that experience has contributed to their leadership development and understanding of issues in their community or country. English Ability Applicants should have sufficient English proficiency to live and study abroad and actively participate in the programme. English will be particularly important for lectures, discussions, meetings, presentations, and interaction with other participants. Cultural Adaptability Applicants should have sufficient cultural adaptability to live and study abroad. The programme involves interaction with people from different cultural and professional backgrounds, making openness, adaptability, respect, and intercultural communication important qualities. Ability to Participate Independently Applicants must possess the physical and mental capabilities necessary to fully participate in programme activities without an accompanying person. Candidates should therefore be prepared to participate independently in the full range of programme activities. How the IATSS Forum 2027 Application Process Works Applications are accepted once a year . The selection process consists of two main stages: Document-based screening Interview-based screening Only shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview. The interview schedule varies depending on the applicant s country. Applicants should therefore understand that the interview date and time may differ between countries. Only applicants who are shortlisted will receive notification regarding the interview. For more information, please CLICK HERE Documents Required for the IATSS Forum Application Applicants must submit all required documents through the online application page. The required documents include the following. Application Form Applicants must complete the official Application Form provided by the IATSS Forum. The form can be completed using: Microsoft Word, or PDF Applicants should ensure that all information is complete and accurate before converting and submitting the final document. CLICK HERE Basic Question Form Applicants must complete the Basic Question Form provided as part of the application materials. The application booklet contains instructions explaining how applicants should approach the questions. Applicants should carefully read these instructions before completing the form. Importantly, the IATSS Forum explicitly states that submitting AI-generated text for the Basic Question Form will result in immediate disqualification . Applicants should therefore write their answers themselves and ensure that their responses genuinely reflect their own experiences, perspectives, motivations, and goals. Essay Applicants must also write a short essay on the topic provided in the official application materials. The essay must be completed using the designated form and should follow the instructions contained in the Application Booklet. As with the Basic Question Form, applicants are explicitly warned that AI-generated text submitted for the essay will result in immediate disqualification . Applicants should therefore ensure that the essay represents their own authentic writing and personal experiences. Recommendation Form Applicants must provide one letter of recommendation from their employer . The recommendation should come from the applicant s direct supervisor at their current job . Applicants must use the official Recommendation Form and follow the instructions provided in the Application Booklet. Because the recommendation requires involvement from a current supervisor, applicants should approach their supervisor sufficiently early to ensure that the document can be completed before the application deadline. English Proficiency Certificate Applicants should attach a copy of any relevant certificate demonstrating English proficiency, if applicable. Examples include: TOEFL TOEIC Other recognised English-language proficiency certificates Applicants should carefully review the official application instructions regarding acceptable documentation. Important Rule Regarding AI-Generated Applications One of the most important instructions for the IATSS Forum application concerns artificial intelligence. The programme explicitly states that: Submitting AI-generated text for the Basic Question Form or Essay will result in immediate disqualification. This means applicants should not use AI-generated responses as their submitted answers for these components. Applicants should instead write their responses themselves and ensure that their answers accurately communicate: Their own experiences Their own leadership journey Their own challenges Their own motivations Their own understanding of issues Their own goals Their own reasons for applying This requirement makes authenticity particularly important in preparing the application. Applicants can carefully review the official instructions and application booklet, but their final responses for the Basic Question Form and Essay should be their own work. Language Requirements for Application Documents All submitted application documents must be written in English . Applicants should also ensure that all documents are: Complete Clearly written Legible Properly formatted Submitted in the required format Handwritten forms will not be accepted. Applicants should also be careful when using acronyms. If an acronym is used, applicants must write out the full name the first time it appears . For example: International Association of Traffic and Safety Sciences (IATSS) After introducing the full name, the acronym can then be used throughout the remainder of the document. How to Apply for the IATSS Forum 2027 Applicants should follow the official application process carefully. Step 1: Download the Application Materials Applicants should download the official: Application Booklet Application Form Basic Question Form Essay Form Recommendation Form Other required application materials The Application Booklet should be read carefully before completing the forms because it contains detailed instructions regarding the application requirements. Step 2: Complete All Required Documents Applicants should complete the required documents in English. They should carefully review each form before submission to ensure that no required section has been left incomplete. Applicants should also ensure that the information provided is consistent across all documents. Step 3: Prepare the Documents for Online Submission Applicants should convert their completed Word documents into PDF format before uploading them. Scanned image files such as JPEG and PNG may also be accepted when they are clear and appropriately sized. However, applicants are advised not to submit photographs of printed documents taken with a smartphone or camera . The programme explains that such photographs may lose accuracy and readability when enlarged. Applicants should therefore use properly scanned documents wherever possible. Step 4: Rename the Files Before uploading the documents, applicants must rename their files by adding their nickname to the beginning of the file name. For example: Abby_Application Form This helps organize the submitted materials and should be completed before proceeding to the online application page. Step 5: Sign in to a Google Account Applicants need to sign in to a Google account to access the online application page. Applicants who do not already have a Google account will need to create one. The programme recommends using Google Chrome while signed in to the relevant Google account for optimal viewing. Step 6: Upload the Documents Online Once all required documents are prepared in PDF or acceptable image formats, applicants should upload them through the appropriate online application page corresponding to their nationality. Applicants are advised to use a PC rather than a mobile device when submitting their application. The application system allows progress to be automatically saved as a draft for 30 days from the applicant s last edit . If an applicant cannot complete the application in one sitting, they should make sure to sign in again using the same Google account to continue working on the application. Step 7: Submit the Application After uploading all required documents and completing the online application, applicants should review the submission carefully before finalizing it. Applicants should avoid uploading multiple sets of the same documents. The IATSS Forum specifically warns that submitting multiple sets may delay processing or result in an applicant missing an opportunity to be considered. Postal Submission The primary application process is online. However, applicants who wish to submit their documents by post should contact their country secretariat in advance . The relevant contact details are provided on the last page of the Application Booklet. Applicants should therefore not send documents by post without first contacting the appropriate country secretariat. Email Applications Are Not Accepted Applicants should be aware that applications submitted by email are not accepted . The required documents must be submitted through the official online application process unless an alternative submission arrangement has been discussed with the relevant country secretariat. Important Application Instructions to Remember Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully review the following requirements: The application deadline is 30 September 2026 . Applications are accepted once a year. Applicants must be 35 years old or younger as of the application closing date. Applicants must currently be working full-time in a professional field, with self-employed and freelance professionals also eligible. Applicants should have at least two years of full-time professional experience. All documents must be written in English. Handwritten forms are not accepted. AI-generated text submitted for the Basic Question Form or Essay results in immediate disqualification. Applicants should provide one recommendation from their direct supervisor at their current job. English proficiency certificates should be provided if applicable. Applicants must carefully follow the instructions in the Application Booklet.
